title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES 12TH CONVOCATION OF ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES AND DR RAM MANOHAR LOHIA HOSPITAL
subtitle: COLLABORATION AMONG HUMAN MEDICINE, VETERINARY MEDICINE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE IS ESSENTIAL FOR ACHIEVING THE GOAL OF ONE HEALTH: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 2:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the 12th convocation of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in New Delhi today (November 20, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that today the concept of 'One Health' is of paramount importance in the field of global health. Due to the constant contact between humans, animals, plants, and the environment, a health issue arising in one domain can affect others as well. Many infectious diseases spread from animals to humans, while air and water pollution, climate change, and environmental imbalances also pose serious challenges to human health. It is, therefore, essential to work in collaboration with experts from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine, and environmental science. This integrated approach will not only facilitate disease prevention and timely detection but also enhance our preparedness to address future health crises.
The President said that understanding the social, economic, nutritional, and environmental conditions is crucial for the prevention and treatment of diseases, as these factors have a direct impact on human health. Research into treatment and preventive measures tailored to local health challenges and circumstances should be encouraged.
The President said that, in assessing the evolving health needs, the Government of India has revised the Health Policy in 2017. Within this comprehensive and inclusive Health Policy, greater emphasis was placed on preventive and promotive services, alongside curative solutions. The focus on rehabilitative and palliative care was also strengthened.  In view of the rapid rise of non-communicable diseases such as mental stress, diabetes, and cancer, special emphasis is being placed on various aspects related to their prevention.
President said that the initiatives undertaken by the Government of India in the health sector over the past decade are yielding far-reaching effects. These have led to a significant expansion of healthcare services, spanning from primary to tertiary levels.
The President told graduating doctors that through their research and efforts, healthcare services can become more effective, accessible, affordable, and people-centric. She underlined that their expertise should also benefit marginalized communities in remote areas, as well as the country’s primary healthcare services. Their thinking and actions should be such that the benefits of their skills can reach the underprivileged sections of society.

subtitle:

Technology must serve humanity and remain guided by constitutional values: Vice President

content:
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 5th Edition of Constitution Week Celebrations 2026, organised by the School of Law, Bennett University, at the Constitution Club of India, New Delhi.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 5th Edition of Constitution Week 2026, organised by the School of Law, Bennett University, at the Constitution Club of India, New Delhi.

Addressing the gathering, he said that the Constitution is much more than a legal document; it is the moral compass of our Republic. He emphasised that constitutional values must become part of everyday public life and that duties are as important as rights.

Highlighting India’s achievements over the last decade, he described them as a silent revolution, translating constitutional aspirations into tangible improvements in people’s lives.

Union Minister Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Attorney General for India, Shri R. Venkataramani; Chancellor, Bennett University and MD, Times Group, Shri Vineet Jain; and Vice-Chancellor, Bennett University, Dr. Raj Singh, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 20, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said that the Constitution of India is much more than a legal document; it is the moral compass of the Republic. He said that constitutional values must not remain confined to institutions and legal texts but must become an integral part of everyday public life. He observed that democracy flourishes when institutions remain accountable, dissent is respected, and citizens exercise their rights and duties responsibly. He stressed that duties deserve as much importance as rights, observing that responsible discharge of duties is essential to safeguarding the rights of all citizens.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s definition of democracy as a form of government through which revolutionary changes in the economic and social life of people are brought about without bloodshed. He said that India’s achievements over the last decade reflect the realisation of constitutional aspirations through tangible improvements in people’s lives. Citing the lifting of around 50 crore people out of poverty, the construction of four crore pucca houses for the poor, and rural tap water coverage crossing 82 per cent under the Jal Jeevan Mission, he said that even border villages, once at the lowest rung of development, are now emerging as vibrant villages. He observed that these achievements represent a silent revolution made possible under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.
Highlighting women’s participation in nation-building, the Vice-President recalled the valuable contributions of the 15 women members of the Constituent Assembly. He noted that their vision is being carried forward through initiatives such as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. He also expressed happiness at witnessing the growing participation of women and their achievements across the country. Describing this progress as another revolution, he said India is steadily moving from women’s development to women-led development, with women becoming active participants in shaping the nation’s destiny.
Speaking about the dynamism of the Constitution, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan cited Article 21, which has evolved over the years to encompass a wide range of rights relating to dignity, livelihood, health, shelter, privacy, education and environmental protection.He called for a balanced approach towards development and environmental conservation, emphasising that natural resources must be utilised to improve living standards while ensuring their sustainability for future generations. He cautioned against mindless consumerism and stressed the need for responsible consumption. He called for greater public awareness about sustainable lifestyles.
The Vice President said that India’s constitutional jurisprudence has made significant contributions to global environmental thought by recognising environmental protection as an integral part of sustainable development. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s initiative, Mission LiFE, he said it inspires individuals and communities across the world to adopt environmentally responsible lifestyles.
Referring to India’s progress in digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence and technological innovation, the Vice President underscored that technology must serve humanity and remain guided by constitutional values. Innovation, he said, should empower citizens, strengthen transparency and expand access to opportunities.He highlighted the important role of universities and institutions of higher learning in this journey, observing that legal education must go beyond professional competence. He said that it should cultivate constitutional sensitivity, ethical leadership, critical thinking and a deeper understanding of social realities.
Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan urged the students to become informed and responsible citizens who engage in reasoned dialogue and contribute constructively to democratic institutions. As India moves towards Viksit Bharat @2047, he said, constitutional values must remain the foundation of the nation’s progress.He concluded by calling upon everyone to strengthen the Constitution through the values they practise and the responsibilities they discharge.
Union Minister of State for Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Attorney General for India, Shri R. Venkataramani; Chancellor, Bennett University and Managing Director, Times Group, Shri Vineet Jain; and Vice-Chancellor, Bennett University, Dr. Raj Singh, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum
subtitle:
Empires may have redrawn the maps of the world, but civilisational dialogues have transformed and enriched global thought; Therefore, the SCO Civilisational Summit is not merely a ceremonial platform;it can become a platform to give direction to the world: PM

21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity in the world;  Along the routes where our ancestors once had to travel for months, today people of those very countries can connect with one another in just a few seconds: PM

Digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange, and international collaboration easier than ever before; SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities: PM

A priceless heritage of thousands of years is preserved across the museums, libraries, and archives of our nations;  Ancient manuscripts, rare texts, historical documents, and artefacts illuminate the many facets of our deep-rooted ties; Today, technology offers tremendous opportunities to pass this heritage on to the younger generation: PM

We can collaborate on the digitisation and translation of ancient texts, and through joint research projects, uncover new dimensions of our shared history; This will enable youth in any part of the world to gain a far deeper understanding of another nation's cultural heritage: PM

Our culture has taught us 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', meaning this entire world is our family; Therefore, here, the aspiration for our own welfare is deeply intertwined in the spirit of global welfare; We consider mutual harmony to be the basis of global wellbeing: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, he welcomed dignitaries, SCO ministers, ambassadors, high commissioners, scholars, artists, and guests from across SCO member states, highlighting the significance of holding a dialogue on civilizational connections at a time when global discussions are dominated by war and unrest, and noting that cultural connect serves as the strongest guarantee for world peace and builds upon the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's 25th anniversary and growing cooperation in security, economy, and connectivity. “Our shared civilizational experiences will play an important role in uniting the world,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the historic setting of Purana Qila,a cultural heritage site whose history scholars trace back thousands of years to the Mahabharata era, the Prime Minister noted how grand cultural performances, energetic Vedic recitations, Buddhist philosophy presentations, and depictions of Hanuman ji's journey at the ancient venue showcased Indian culture alongside universal messages of love, unity, and human welfare that transcend geopolitical borders. “You all will also enjoy this event, and by making it historic, will also lay the foundation of a new tradition for which the future will remember all of you,” remarked PM Modi.
Tracing centuries-old international collaboration and people-to-people ties from trade links between the Indus Valley Civilization and Mesopotamia around five thousand years ago to Silk and trade networks connecting India, China, Central Asia, and Eurasia,where merchants, scholars, travelers, and Buddhist monks such as Faxian, Xuanzang, Yijing, and Kucha-born Kumarajiva, alongside institutions like Nalanda and centers like Kucha and Dunhuang, enriched civilizations through exchanges of ideas, languages, and Buddhist texts,the Prime Minister underscored the enduring power of cultural dialogue. “Empires have certainly changed the maps of the world, but civilizational dialogues have changed the ideas of the world and enriched them,” asserted Shri Modi.
Observing that as knowledge travels across regions, its expression may evolve while its illuminating impact remains constant, the Prime Minister cited how India's Panchatantra traveled to Persian and Arabic as Kalila wa Dimna to become immortal across generations and how the Ramayana enriched local culture, performing arts, and literature in Southeast Asia as Reamker in Cambodia. “Knowledge, in whichever form it exists, spreads light alone,” remarked PM Modi.
Highlighting the importance of cross-cultural exchange in science and mathematics, the Prime Minister noted how the mathematical ideas of Indian scholar Brahmagupta reached Baghdad. “There, scholars like Al-Khwarizmi made an important contribution in taking the knowledge of mathematics forward,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing to shared legacies in architecture and music,including links between Central Asian Maqam and Indian Raga traditions, Sufi influences enriching Qawwali in India, and Central Asian garden traditions from Samarkand and Herat shaping the Charbagh style,the Prime Minister stressed the value of sustaining open cultural exchanges. “That this exchange continues in a free flow even today, for that, the role of this summit and of such initiatives becomes important,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that 21st-century technology has unlocked unprecedented opportunities for cultural connectivity,enabling people across regions that once required months of travel to connect within seconds while digital platforms streamline knowledge sharing, cultural exchange, and international collaboration,the Prime Minister called for leveraging these advancements. “SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities,” asserted Shri Modi.
Sharing suggestions with the gathered guests on preserving and sharing thousands of years of heritage housed in museums, libraries, and archives,such as ancient manuscripts, rare texts, historical documents, and artifacts,the Prime Minister proposed cooperation in digitizing and translating ancient texts as well as joint research projects on shared history. “Because of this, a youth sitting in any part of the world will be able to understand the cultural heritage of another country in a much better way,” observed PM Modi.
Noting that many great literary and intellectual works remain available in limited languages despite expanded resources today, the Prime Minister pointed to technological tools for broadening access. “With the help of AI, new momentum can be given to their translation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting additional avenues for cultural exchange,including joint exhibitions by museums and cultural institutions, scholar and researcher exchanges between universities, heritage circuits and cultural routes linking Silk Route and Buddhist heritage sites, cultural tourism, joint cultural festivals, and artist exchanges,the Prime Minister expressed confidence in the human impact of such initiatives. “Through such efforts, our citizens will get opportunities to know and understand each other's culture even more closely,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Stressing that the responsibility of carrying today's civilizational dialogue to new heights in coming decades rests with younger generations who are tech-savvy and eager to understand the world, the Prime Minister called for greater opportunities for youth to engage with diverse languages, literature, and cultural traditions while involving local artists and artisans. “Our young artists, writers, and filmmakers, through digital media and other creative platforms, can convey our shared heritage to the new generation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Recalling that Indian prayers at the conclusion of rituals seek goodwill among all beings and welfare for the entire world rooted in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, treating the whole world as one family, the Prime Minister linked individual and national wellbeing to global harmony. “We consider mutual goodwill itself as the base of global wellbeing,” affirmed PM Modi.
Observing that mutual goodwill depends on mutual trust built around shared commonalities, the Prime Minister drew on India's experience of embracing and celebrating diversity across varied languages, lifestyles, and traditions,inspired by the Vedic recitation heard at the start of the forum, to turn plurality into unity. “When we adopt this generous perspective, then our diversity itself becomes the basis of our unity,” asserted Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by invoking the Vedic call ‘Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manansi Janatam’ to walk together, converse together, and achieve harmony of thoughts, the Prime Minister extended congratulations on the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum and best wishes for productive deliberations.

title: English rendering of PM's address at the inauguration of First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
His Excellency the Secretary General of the SCO, India's Minister of Culture, other Ministers of the Government of India, all Ministers, Ambassadors, High Commissioners, Dignitaries, Distinguished Scholars, eminent artists, esteemed guests from SCO countries, ladies and gentlemen.
This is the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum. I welcome all the guests who have come to India and extend my greetings to all of you. At a time when discussions around the world are dominated by war and unrest, we are holding a dialogue in India on civilizational connections. This is especially important because cultural connection is the strongest guarantee of global peace. Therefore, the significance of today's event has become even greater.
Friends,
Only a few months ago, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation completed 25 years of its establishment. Over the years, the SCO has significantly expanded cooperation in security, economy, and connectivity. In such a situation, cultural and civilizational cooperation will further strengthen relations among different countries. I am confident that this forum will generate new ideas, create new opportunities for cultural cooperation, and that our shared civilizational experiences will play an important role in bringing the world together.
Friends,
At this moment, we are at Delhi's Purana Qila. This Purana Qila is an extraordinary cultural heritage of India. Its history is as fascinating as the stories associated with it. You may have already read and heard about it here. According to scholars, the history of this fort goes back thousands of years to the era of the Mahabharata. At such an ancient site, magnificent cultural performances, the energetic recitation of Vedic mantras, presentations of Buddhist philosophy, and the journey of Hanuman Ji not only reflected India's culture but also conveyed a message of love and unity for humanity.
These emotions, these ideas, and these teachings are as ancient as they are universal. Beyond geopolitical boundaries, they naturally connect us with one another. This is also the purpose of this summit, and it is also the need of the present time. I hope all of you will enjoy this event and, by making it historic, will lay the foundation of a new tradition. A tradition for which the future will remember all of you.
Today, there is a great deal of discussion around international collaboration and people-to-people connect. This is an approach that our ancestors enriched over many centuries. Around five thousand years ago, there were trade relations between the Indus Valley Civilization and Mesopotamia. Later, other trade routes further expanded this contact. India, China, Central Asia, and many regions of Eurasia were connected through these ancient trade networks. Along these routes travelled not only merchants, but also scholars, travellers, and Buddhist monks. These journeys facilitated the exchange of ideas, languages, and traditions. Through Gandhara and Central Asia, the ideas contained in Buddhist texts reached China. Places such as Kucha and Dunhuang became important centres of this journey. Scholars such as Faxian, Xuanzang, and Yijing came to India from China. They studied India's traditions of knowledge and carried them back to their homeland. Universities such as Nalanda became centres of this exchange of knowledge. Scholars such as Kumarajiva, who was born in Kucha in Central Asia, translated Buddhist texts into Chinese. In this way, humanity and civilization continued to enrich and develop themselves. I believe that empires may have changed the map of the world, but civilizational dialogues changed the ideas of the world and strengthened intellectual prosperity. Therefore, the SCO Civilizational Summit is not merely a ceremonial platform; it can become a platform for giving direction to the world.
Friends,
When knowledge travels from one place to another, the way it is expressed may change, but its impact and its role do not change. Whatever form knowledge takes, it spreads light. A major example of this is India's Panchatantra. Its stories travelled into Persian and later into Arabic. In the form of Kalila wa Dimna, these stories assumed a new shape and became immortal across generations. Similarly, when the Ramayana travelled from India to Southeast Asia, it strengthened the same ideals there. In Cambodia, the Ramayana took the form of Reamker and found a place in local culture, performing arts, and literature.
Friends,
This cross-cultural exchange has been equally important in the fields of science and mathematics. The ideas of the great Indian mathematician Brahmagupta reached Baghdad. There, scholars such as Al-Khwarizmi made significant contributions in advancing mathematical knowledge.
Friends,
We find many examples of this shared journey in architecture and music as well. There is a deep cultural connection between the Maqam traditions of Central Asia and the Raga traditions of India. Sufi ideas and musical traditions enriched the development of Qawwali in India. The garden traditions of Samarkand and Herat in Central Asia influenced the Charbagh style in India. For these exchanges to continue flowing freely even today, the role of this summit and such initiatives becomes extremely important.
Friends,
Today, we have far greater opportunities than ever before. The technology of the 21st century has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity across the world. The routes on which our ancestors once had to travel for months now connect people from those same countries with one another in just a few seconds. Digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange, and international collaboration easier than ever before. The countries of the SCO should take full advantage of these new opportunities.
Friends,
Today, I would also like to offer a few suggestions in this direction before all of you distinguished guests. In the museums, libraries, and archives of our countries, invaluable heritage accumulated over thousands of years has been preserved. Ancient manuscripts, rare texts, historical documents, and artefacts reveal many dimensions of our shared connections. Today, technology provides excellent opportunities to bring this heritage to younger generations. We can cooperate in the digitisation and translation of ancient texts. Through joint research projects, we can bring new dimensions of our shared history before the world. This will enable a young person sitting in any part of the world to better understand the cultural heritage of another country.
Friends,
Many of our great literary works are still available only in limited languages. With the help of AI, the translation of these works can be accelerated significantly. Today we have more tools than ever before, and we should make full use of them.
Friends,
There are many more opportunities for cultural exchange that deserve our attention. For example, museums and cultural institutions in our countries can organise joint exhibitions. Universities and research institutions can promote exchange programmes for scholars and researchers. Cultural tourism can also become an important area of cooperation among us. Many historical sites linked to the Silk Routes and Buddhist heritage exist across our countries. We can explore possibilities for connecting them through heritage circuits and cultural routes. Similarly, joint cultural festivals and artists' exchange programmes can bring our art and cultural traditions to new audiences. I believe such efforts will give our citizens better opportunities to understand each other's cultures more closely.
Friends,
The responsibility for taking forward this civilizational dialogue that we are advancing today to even greater heights in the coming decades rests with our youth. Today's younger generation is connected through technology and wants to understand the world better. We must provide more opportunities for our youth to connect with each other's languages, literature, and cultural traditions. Our young artists, writers, and filmmakers can take our shared heritage to future generations through digital media and other creative platforms. We must also connect local artists and artisans to these efforts.
Friends,
In India, even when we perform a prayer or a ritual, we conclude by praying: May there be goodwill among all living beings. May the world be blessed. This is because our culture has taught us the ideal of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - the whole world is one family. Therefore, the desire for our own well-being is inseparably linked with the well-being of the world. We regard mutual harmony as the foundation of global well-being.
Friends,
The most important requirement for mutual harmony is mutual trust. And mutual trust develops when we feel that we share something with one another. Therefore, today there is a need to focus on what is shared among us. From India’s experience, I can say that when we adopt such a broad outlook, our diversity itself becomes the foundation of our unity. That is why, despite our many languages, lifestyles, and traditions, we remain deeply connected in India. In India, we accept diversity. We celebrate diversity. We derive this inspiration hi from our Vedas, whose recitation we listened to at the beginning of this programme.
Friends,
Our Vedas say: Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manamsi Janatam - let us walk together, let us engage in dialogue, and let there be harmony in our thoughts. With this spirit, I once again congratulate all of you on the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum. Being the first, it carries special significance. I extend my best wishes to all of you for successful and meaningful discussions.
Thank you very much.
Namaskar.

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Bihar on 21 November 2026. At around 1:15 PM, the Prime Minister will visit Nitish Setu in Vaishali district. Thereafter, at around 2 PM, he will inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects and lay the foundation stone of several projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore  in Vaishali. The projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare, transport and other important sectors, and are aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public services across the state.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation Nitish Setu, an extradosed cable-stayed bridge over the River Ganga, built at a cost of around Rs. 4,280 crore. The 19.7 km-long project connects Kachhi Dargah on NH-22 in Patna district with Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali district. It comprises a 9.7 km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads.
The bridge will provide an important additional crossing over River Ganga, easing traffic pressure on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu and reducing travel time between North and South Bihar. It will particularly benefit residents of Raghopur Diara by improving their access to Patna and essential services such as healthcare and education. The project will also facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and industrial goods, improve access to markets and promote trade and commerce across the region, contributing to Bihar's economic development.
Prime Minister will inaugurate several major infrastructure and development projects worth over Rs. 15,600 crore. Major road projects include the six-laning of the Aurangabad-Chordaha section of NH-19, the Chorma-Bairgania section of NH-227F and the Umagaon-Saharsa section of NH-327, among others.
In the power sector, Prime Minister will inaugurate Unit 2 (660 MW) of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with electricity distribution and transmission infrastructure projects under the Energy Department. These include RDSS Loss Reduction Works worth over Rs. 1,130 crore among others. Other projects to be inaugurated include restoration and strengthening of canals and embankments, a floating solar project at Phulwaria Dam in Nawada and sewerage infrastructure at Kahalgaon. Prime Minister will also inaugurate buildings and facilities for educational institutions, residential schools, health services, agriculture, sports and public administration. These projects will contribute to improved irrigation, urban services and access to essential facilities.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of several projects worth around Rs. 14,450 crore. Prominent among these are the four-laning of the Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah section of NH-139W, to be developed at a cost of over Rs. 3,800 crore, and the power evacuation project for the Pirpainti Super Thermal Power Project (3 x 800 MW), estimated at around Rs. 3,350 crore.
Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone of sewerage and water-supply projects in Begusarai, Biharsharif, Purnea, Hajipur, Motihari, Danapur, Khagaria, Samastipur, Bodhgaya, Sitamarhi, Saharsa and other urban areas. Other projects include modernisation of canal systems, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Residential Schools, the IIT Patna Research Park and hostel, engineering and polytechnic institutions, and emergency response and police data centre infrastructure, among others.
Prime Minister will flag off 100 PM-eBuses, giving a further boost to cleaner public transport in the State. Griha Pravesh of over 26,900 beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) will also be held, marking an important milestone in providing housing to urban families.

content:
New Delhi, 20 November 2026
: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today called upon the Defence Estates Organisation to strengthen the management and protection of defence land through modern technology, digitisation, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Addressing the centenary celebrations of the Defence Estates Organisation in New Delhi, he emphasised that securing defence assets, curbing encroachments, and ensuring timely land availability for the operational needs of the Armed Forces must remain top priorities.
Highlighting the scale of the organisation’s mandate in managing and safeguarding more than 1.7 million acres of defence land, Shri Birla underlined that accurate, secure, and accessible land records are vital for effective governance. He commended the digital upgrades already underway and noted that AI and emerging technologies will help address both present operational demands and long-term administrative challenges.
Pointing to encroachment on defence land as a key concern, Shri Birla appreciated the organization’s efforts to protect properties and carry out accurate surveys and measurements, while taking care to avoid unnecessary disputes or hardship for civilians. He also stressed that timely access to land and conducive conditions for defence establishments and personnel are essential to national security.
Speaking on the historical and ecological value of cantonments, Shri Birla noted that their original character, green cover, forests, and heritage must be protected as they adapt to modern needs. Development, he cautioned, should be planned thoughtfully so that the distinct identity of military cantonments is preserved amid rapid urban growth.
He lauded the organization’s civic initiatives for cantonment residents—including schools, healthcare facilities, computer education, skill training, water conservation and recycling, and environmental protection—and called for sustained engagement with civil society to respond to evolving community needs.
Emphasizing institutional continuity, Shri Birla encouraged officers and staff to study the laws, rules, and administrative frameworks built over the past century, and to learn from former officers. Pairing this institutional wisdom with the technical agility of younger personnel, he said, will build stronger systems for the future.
Shri Birla observed that as the Defence Estates Organisation enters its second century, the focus must be on building an institution that combines its rich legacy with a forward-looking vision. Shri Birla expressed confidence that, through innovation, transparency, technological advancement and a renewed commitment to public service, the Organisation will continue to safeguard the nation’s valuable defence land, strengthen the operational preparedness of the Armed Forces and preserve the unique heritage of its cantonments. He called upon all officers and employees to carry this responsibility forward with dedication, foresight and a shared sense of national purpose.

title: India Takes a Historic Leap Towards Self-Reliance: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Dedicates Country’s First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine to the Nation in Bhopal
subtitle:
A befitting response to those who malign India abroad: Shri Chouhan says the world must see the new, self-reliant and developed India

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Announces ₹300-Crore State-of-the-Art Animal Disease Research Laboratory in Bhopal

Indigenous Bird Flu Vaccine to Protect Poultry Farmers from Disease Outbreaks at Just ₹1-2 per Dose: Shri Chouhan

Shri Chouhan Salutes Scientists for Months of Research and Unprecedented Commitment in Developing Indigenous Bird Flu Vaccine

Shri Chouhan Highlights India's Progress in Animal Disease Control, Credits National Vaccination Drive for Major Gains

Shri Chouhan Hits Back at Critics Questioning India's Institutions and Scientific Achievements, Says Country's Progress Speaks for Itself
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major milestone for India's scientific capabilities and the country's drive towards self-reliance, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today dedicated India's first indigenous chicken vaccine against Avian Influenza (H5N1), commonly known as bird flu, to the nation at a program in Bhopal. On the occasion, the Union Minister announced the establishment of a new state-of-the-art laboratory in Bhopal at an estimated cost of ₹300 crore. He also took a dig at opposition leaders for questioning India's constitutional institutions and the capabilities of its scientists while speaking abroad. Priced at an affordable ₹1-2 per dose, the vaccine is the world's first vaccine against this particular variant of bird flu. It is expected to strengthen disease prevention in the poultry sector, protect the livelihoods of millions of poultry farmers and help reduce the enormous economic losses caused by animal diseases.
Those who malign India abroad must see the new, self-reliant India
Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan took aim at opposition leaders who, he said, seek to discredit the country on international platforms. He said that those who go abroad and malign their own country must take note of India's achievements and its growing scientific capabilities. He said that people who hold constitutional positions but question the Constitution abroad, undermine constitutional institutions and cast doubts on the contribution of India's armed forces, scientists and hardworking citizens must look at the changing India of today. Shri Chouhan recalled that Indian scientists had earlier surprised the world by developing two indigenous COVID-19 vaccines in just nine months through a task force constituted under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The development of the country's first indigenous bird flu vaccine is another demonstration of India's scientific strength and self-reliance, he added.
₹300-crore state-of-the-art laboratory to come up in Bhopal
Highlighting the achievements of the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal, Shri Chouhan announced a new state-of-the-art laboratory worth ₹300 crore for the city. He said that the Bhopal-based institute had emerged as a symbol of India's scientific excellence. The Minister also explained why the vaccine was dedicated to the nation in Bhopal rather than Delhi. Although there had initially been a proposal to launch the vaccine from Delhi, he decided that the occasion should take place in Bhopal, among the scientists who had worked day and night to develop it and in the presence of the people of the city. The achievement belonged to these scientists, and it was important to recognise their contribution at the very place where the vaccine had been developed, he said.
Livestock are 'moving ATMs' for farmers; indigenous vaccines to help prevent annual losses of ₹56,000 crore
Describing animal husbandry and poultry as vital pillars of the rural economy, Shri Chouhan said that livestock are 'moving ATMs' for farmers, providing a regular source of monthly income alongside agriculture. He highlighted that animal husbandry contributes 14 per cent to India's GDP, while the poultry sector accounts for another 1 per cent. He also underlined the substantial economic burden caused by major animal diseases. According to the figures shared by the Minister, Foot and Mouth Disease causes average annual losses of ₹22,000 crore, Lumpy Skin Disease results in losses of ₹20,000 crore, Brucellosis accounts for ₹9,212 crore and Peste des Petits Ruminants, a disease affecting sheep and goats, causes losses of ₹4,683 crore. Together, these diseases have caused losses of approximately ₹56,000 crore to the country and its farmers. Indigenous vaccines are playing a crucial role in protecting livestock, safeguarding farmers' incomes and reducing this economic burden, he said.
Vaccine priced at just ₹1-2 per dose; India has witnessed over 500 bird flu outbreaks since 2006
Shri Chouhan recalled that India's first bird flu outbreak was reported in 2006 in Navapur, Maharashtra, resulting in the death of 10 lakh chickens. To contain the infection, lakhs of additional birds had to be culled and buried. Subsequently, around 9 lakh chickens died in 2021, while another 2 lakh died this year. Since 2006, India has witnessed more than 500 bird flu outbreaks, causing significant damage to the poultry industry. The disease also poses a risk of transmission to mammals and humans, making effective prevention and control measures particularly important. The new indigenous vaccine has been priced at just ₹1-2 per dose to ensure that even small poultry farmers can afford it. Its low cost will make preventive vaccination more accessible and help protect the livelihoods of poultry farmers across the country, the Minister said.
National vaccination drive delivering decisive results against animal diseases
Shri Chouhan highlighted the government's sustained efforts to control major animal diseases through vaccination. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the National Animal Disease Control Program from Mathura, the land of Lord Krishna, to strengthen disease prevention and protect livestock. Under the program, 147 crore 16 lakh free vaccine doses have so far been administered against Foot and Mouth Disease. Brucellosis has also been brought under control, he said. Recalling the outbreak of Lumpy Skin Disease in 2022, Shri Chouhan said that 32 lakh 80 thousand animals were infected and 1 lakh 86 thousand animals lost their lives. Scientists at Hisar and Izatnagar subsequently developed the 'Lumpi-ProVacInd' vaccine to combat the disease. He also commended the achievements of ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, which has previously developed indigenous vaccines for Gumboro disease, Brucella abortus S-19 Delta, Classical Swine Fever and African Swine Fever. The latest H5N1 vaccine adds another significant achievement to the institute's contribution to India's animal health research.
Scientists worked through holidays and followed stringent biosafety protocols to develop the vaccine
Paying tribute to the scientists behind the vaccine, Shri Chouhan described them as the real heroes of this achievement and praised their extraordinary commitment and dedication. The research team comprised Dr. S. Nagarajan, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Dr. C. Tosh, Dr. H. V. Murugkar, Dr. Aniket Sanyal, Dr. Senthil Kumar D., Dr. Naveen Kumar and Dr. Yogisharadhya R. The Minister shared that the scientists worked continuously for months, foregoing their Saturday and Sunday holidays to complete the research. Their work also required strict adherence to demanding biosafety protocols. As part of these protocols, they had to undergo sanitisation procedures before and after leaving the laboratory, use 120 litres of water daily for bathing and refrain from keeping any pets at home throughout the research period. Shri Chouhan saluted their commitment, describing their dedication as being akin to the discipline and sacrifice of soldiers serving the nation. He said that the achievement reflected the extraordinary perseverance of India's scientific community.
The program was attended by Madhya Pradesh Minister for Youth Welfare, Sports and Cooperation Shri Vishwas Sarang; Bhopal MP Shri Alok Sharma; Khategaon MLA Shri Ashish Sharma; Bhopal Mayor Smt. Malti Rai; senior public representatives Shri Rakesh Sharma, Shri Naresh Mewada, Shri Rakesh Jadon, Shri Rajesh Chouksey and Ms. Chhaya, along with councillors. ICAR Director General Dr. M. L. Jat, NIHSAD Director Dr. Aniket Sanyal, scientists and a large number of distinguished guests were also present.

The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players.
That confidence rests on strong fundamentals. Production from captive and commercial coal mines rose 10.22% to 210.46 million tonnes in FY 2025-26, and coal continues to anchor India’s energy security as demand grows with the economy. Since 2020, 145 coal mines have been auctioned across 15 rounds, bringing in 44 new companies. These mines are expected to generate about Rs. 47,500 crore in annual revenue and around 4.9 lakh jobs. The auction framework adds to the appeal, with no end-use restriction on coal, 100% FDI through the automatic route and low upfront payments.
The bids will now be evaluated by a multi-disciplinary Technical Evaluation Committee. Technically qualified bidders will be shortlisted to participate in the electronic auction on the MSTC portal.
With each round, commercial coal mining draws deeper and wider investor commitment. The strong participation in the current round reinforces the sector’s place at the heart of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047.

title: India's transformation, growing startup ecosystem and opportunities for youth reflect the country's journey towards a developed nation: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal at Annual Convocation of DU
subtitle: Commerce Minister urges graduates to pursue their dreams, remain lifelong learners and shoulder responsibility towards less privileged sections of society
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today addressed the 103rd Annual Convocation of the University of Delhi, calling upon graduates to pursue their dreams, embrace opportunities and contribute to India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. Highlighting India's economic transformation, he said that approximately 50 crore Indians had moved out of extreme poverty over the last decade. From a few hundred startups a decade ago, India had emerged as the world's third-largest startup ecosystem, with 2.5 lakh startups and over 130 unicorns. He said that young Indians were increasingly becoming job creators rather than job seekers, demonstrating a willingness to experiment, accept failure and take on new challenges.
Shri Goyal said that the journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 rested on the shoulders of the country's youth. As graduates progressed in their careers, they would have tremendous opportunities to create a better future for less privileged and marginalised sections of society. He emphasised that their future was intertwined with the future of those who had been left behind and had not received similar opportunities. He urged graduates to remain conscious of their obligations towards these sections and said that the satisfaction of positively impacting even one individual's life was immeasurable.
Congratulating the graduating students and their parents, Shri Goyal said that approximately 2.5 crore young Indians reach college age every year, but very few get the opportunity to study at prestigious institutions such as the University of Delhi. Students had earned their place through board examinations, CUET, mock tests and revisions, and had subsequently navigated the challenges of CGPAs, society auditions, internships and placements. He said that the strong foundation provided by the University would help them build successful careers.
The Minister said that the achievement of the graduating students belonged equally to their parents, who had sacrificed their own dreams to make their children's aspirations possible. He also urged them to remember those who had supported them during their university years, including canteen staff who maintained their accounts, security guards who recognised them without identity cards, librarians who helped them excel in examinations and Sudama ji, the tea seller whose chai had been part of their university experience.
Shri Goyal emphasised the importance of respecting teachers, observing that a teacher's work did not end when the bell rang but continued to influence students' lives for decades. He said that students often recognised the importance of their teachers' guidance, corrections and lessons only after entering the real world and facing life's challenges.
Referring to the University's 104-year journey, Shri Goyal noted that Delhi University had grown to 90 colleges and over six lakh students and had never missed a convocation in its 103-year history. The University had continued its tradition through the freedom struggle, second World War and the COVID pandemic. He said it was a double honour to be present at the convocation, where more than 400 doctoral degrees, over 1.7 lakh bachelor's and master's degrees and more than 160 gold medals were being awarded.
Highlighting the achievements of the University's women students, he said their hard work, perseverance and success reflected the commitment towards ensuring quality education for every girl child in the country. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi would be pleased to learn of these achievements.
The Minister also urged graduates to value the friendships they had formed during their university years. He observed that students often spent more time with their friends than with their families during these formative years. Friends had woken them up for 9 AM examinations, lent them notes and believed in their ideas when nobody else did. He encouraged graduates to keep these friendships close, observing that their friends could become their first clients, partners or investors, while remaining their oldest well-wishers and most honest critics. Encouraging students to remember three words, "Pursue your dreams", Shri Goyal quoted Steve Jobs: "Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. Have courage to follow your heart and intuition."
Sharing six lessons for success, Shri Goyal encouraged graduates to think big, remain positive, maintain focus, continue learning, prioritise their health and trust their struggles.
First, he urged students to think big, dream big and have conviction in their aspirations. He cautioned them against setting small targets or fearing failure and encouraged them to work hard towards achieving their goals. Referring to Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States, he highlighted his difficult childhood, limited formal education and early failures in business and professional life. He said that Lincoln remained an avid reader, maintained a lifelong interest in learning and continued to persevere despite setbacks, eventually becoming President and playing a central role in abolishing slavery in the United States.
Second, he advised students to remain positive and never fear course correction. Citing Thomas Edison's repeated experiments in developing the electric bulb, he said that countless setbacks and years of persistence had ultimately led to success. He encouraged graduates to learn from every attempt, adapt to changing circumstances and modify their approach whenever necessary, while continuing to pursue their dreams.
Third, he emphasised the importance of focus, observing that in a world of 30-second reels, the ability to concentrate had become rare and therefore valuable. Quoting Swami Vivekananda, he said, "Pick up one idea, make that one idea your life." He stressed that maintaining focus on one's aspirations was essential to achieving success.
Fourth, he urged graduates to remain lifelong learners. Referring to the age of Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies, he said that students must remain open to learning and be prepared to unlearn existing practices and rethink their approaches. He emphasised that human experiences were important in solving the problems of tomorrow and that critical thinking was something no one could replace.
Fifth, he advised students to take care of their health, describing the body as the only vehicle that would remain with them throughout life's journey. He observed that young people often took their health for granted, with late nights, parties and irregular habits, but might regret not having developed greater discipline later in life. He encouraged them to build lasting fitness habits through walking, playing, running and yoga, and highlighted the importance of preventive healthcare in preserving the body, mind and soul.
Sixth, he asked graduates to trust their struggles and view hardships as preparation for their destiny. Referring to the 14 years of exile endured by God Ram and the Pandavas' 12 years in the forest followed by one year in disguise, he said that hardships often prepared individuals for their destiny.
Recalling one of his biggest and dearest mentors, former Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Shri Goyal quoted him as saying, "Education, in the truest sense of the term, is the process of self-discovery, art of self-sculpture." He noted that Atal ji had made these remarks at the Golden Jubilee of the University Grants Commission in 2002.
Referring to the five Pran, or five national commitments, outlined by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi from the ramparts of the Red Fort during the 75th Independence Day celebrations, Shri Goyal called upon graduates to make these commitments part of their lives and contribute towards realising them by 2047.
The first Pran was to build a developed India by 2047. Shri Goyal said that a developed India would be one that was prosperous, cared for every child and citizen and provided a good quality of life to every family. He described this as the graduates' job description from the day they left the University.
The second Pran was freedom from the mentality of slavery. Appreciating the University's decision to move away from traditional graduation gowns and robes towards Indian attire, he said that it conveyed a larger message of confidence in India's own identity and traditions. He observed that the change was not merely about the convocation uniform but reflected the confidence of New India to lead with its own mind.
The third Pran was to take pride in India's history, heritage, culture and traditions. Shri Goyal said that no country could develop without respecting its culture and history. Referring to his recent visit to Rome, where he had interacted with Italy's Deputy Prime Minister during a business forum and joint committee meeting, he said that he had also been given a guided tour of Italian art and culture, including a 200-year-old painting and sculpture. He highlighted the importance other countries attached to preserving and showcasing their cultural heritage.
He also referred to the transformation of the North and South Blocks in New Delhi, which had housed government offices for years and had become inefficient due to changing administrative requirements and infrastructure. He said that the two buildings were being developed into the Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum, which would showcase India's thousands of years of history and heritage to the world and strengthen the country's cultural confidence.
The fourth Pran was national unity. Referring to the Statue of Unity dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at Kevadia in Gujarat, Shri Goyal highlighted the development of the surrounding tribal region following the establishment of the statue. He said that the transformation of the area demonstrated the importance of national unity in achieving development. He emphasised that a divided society could never achieve its full potential or secure its rightful place in the world, and urged everyone to remain united and safeguard the unity of the country.
The fifth Pran was a sense of duty. Shri Goyal said that greater power also brought greater responsibility. As graduates left the University with the power of a new degree, they must also carry their duties and responsibilities towards the country. These included contributing to India's development, building a drug-free nation, keeping the environment clean and taking the country forward in the field of technology. He expressed confidence that by 2047, when India celebrated 100 years of Independence, the country would become an example for the world.
The Minister said that the real takeaway from a convocation was the power to craft and sculpt one's future. He expressed confidence that every graduate would leave the University empowered, encouraged and equipped with a vision for the future. Describing the students as national assets with relentless energy, he said that they would shape the destiny of India and make their teachers, parents and the nation proud.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal urged students to learn lessons from history but never be afraid of it. He encouraged them to pursue big dreams and audacious goals despite difficulties and challenges, and to participate enthusiastically in shaping both their own future and the future of India. He said that the energy of the graduating students gave him immense encouragement and confidence.
Wishing the graduates a life filled with enthusiasm and zeal, Shri Goyal congratulated them on their achievements and wished them success in their future endeavours.

title: Hon’ble Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Flags Off ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ from New Delhi
subtitle:
Over 1,100 students embark on a special train journey to Somnath under Somnath Swabhiman Parv

More than 35,000 devotees have visited Somnath under the initiative

Yatra to connect young people with India's historical and spiritual legacy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’, organised under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, was flagged off by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. More than 1,100 students from various colleges and institutions have embarked on this special train journey to Somnath, Gujarat.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that despite repeated attacks over a thousand years, the Somnath Temple continues to stand as a symbol of India's enduring cultural heritage. He highlighted how earlier generations protected not only their faith but also the country's rich traditions and heritage. He said that the history of Somnath reflects India's faith, resilience and cultural continuity.
Addressing the young participants, the Minister said that this is not an ordinary journey but an opportunity to understand India's history of struggle and resilience, and to carry forward its glorious legacy. He encouraged the students to take pride in India's intellectual wealth, architectural heritage and cultural achievements, which have influenced the world and continue to do so.
Under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, more than 35,000 devotees have so far had the opportunity to visit Somnath Mahadev. The initiative highlights the historical and cultural significance of the Somnath Temple and its enduring place in India's heritage.
Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Samar Nanda said, “Under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, devotees from 17 states have visited Somnath Mahadev. The 75th anniversary of the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple was also commemorated on 11 May 2026 in the presence of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Yuva Somnath Yatra is an important initiative to connect the younger generation with Somnath and its rich historical and spiritual significance.”
Before the departure of the train, Sadho Band presented devotional musical performances at the railway station, creating a spiritual and enthusiastic atmosphere. The devotional performances filled the young participants with enthusiasm and added to the spirit of the occasion.
A ceremonial Guard of Honour was also presented by NCC women cadets, adding to the significance of the occasion.
The initiative aims to connect the younger generation with India's rich cultural heritage and historical legacy, while creating greater awareness about the historical significance of Somnath.
Scheduled from 20 to 25 November 2026, the special train will travel from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi, to Veraval Junction in Gujarat. From there, the students will proceed to Somnath to experience the historical and spiritual significance of the revered temple.

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has revised its earlier notification dated 07th September 2020 regarding methodology for calculation of Local Content / Domestic Value Addition (DVA) for Six IT-Hardware products under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017, with a view to promoting domestic manufacturing, strengthening indigenous capabilities and generating employment.
The revised methodology covers the following Six Products:
Desktop PCs / All-in-One PCs (AIO-PCs)
Laptop PCs
Thin Clients
Servers
Computer Monitors and
Interactive Flat Panel Displays (IFPDs).
The revised framework introduces a process-oriented, Bill of Materials (BoM)-based mechanism for computation of DVA. It recognises eligible manufacturing activities & processes undertaken in India, including mainboard/motherboard assembly through Surface Mount Technology (SMT), domestic sourcing of bare PCB, assembly, testing and packaging of memory (RAM) and storage (SSD), display assembly processes, domestic sourcing of chassis and power module, and final assembly and testing.
The revised methodology provides adequate weightage to eligible in-house Research and Development (R&D) undertaken in India to promote indigenous technology development and innovation.
Further, to encourage and promote indigenous design capability and creation of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) of such IT hardware products, additional weightage has been assigned to Indian product design and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR).
The revised methodology also provides a standardised format for DVA calculation and self-certification to ensure objectivity and transparency in DVA assessment made by the manufacturers. This would also enable objective verification of the self-declared DVA by manufacturers, wherever required.
The revised methodology shall come into effect six months from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette and shall supersede the corresponding provisions of MeitY's notification dated 07th September 2020 for these six products.

title: MeitY Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on Digital Accessibility and Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities
subtitle: Dialogue Highlights Accessibility Standards, Assistive Tools and Inclusive Digital Public Services
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 10:40AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) held an interactive session with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on advancing digital accessibility and inclusion in India. The engagement, held at CeG Hall, MeitY, formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India from November 16-25, 2026. In addition to MeitY officials,
the Ministry
of External Affairs also took part, along with representatives of National Informatics Centre (NIC),
Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification
(
STQC), Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and National e-Governance Division (NeGD).
The session was led by Shri Nand Kumarum, Joint Secretary, MeitY, and President & CEO, NeGD. It began with a short film on Hon’ble PM’s vision on accessibility along with India’s digital accessibility initiatives, followed by a detailed presentation and discussion.
Thereafter, a presentation was given jointly by Dr. Santosh Pandey, Scientist-E, Meity and Shri Bramhanand Jha, VP, NeGD. It outlined how India’s legal framework supports digital accessibility. India ratified the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2007, and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 requires accessible information and communication technology. MeitY notified the National Policy on Universal Electronic Accessibility in 2013, and its role is largely facilitative, through standards, guidelines and tools.
Key initiatives discussed including:
Standards:
GIGW 3.0, the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps, aligned with WCAG
2.1 Level AA; and Indian Standard IS 17802 on accessibility of ICT products and services, made enforceable through the RPwD Rules by the 2023 amendment.
Certification and testing:
STQC certification, with 73 Ministries and Departments certified; and tools such as SugamyaWeb and SATYA for testing websites and apps.
Design support:
UX4G, which has given UX audit and design support to over 400 government websites and apps, and whose ready-to-use accessibility widget is used by over 1,800 websites.
Inclusive services:
Bhashini for multilingual access, UMANG for citizen services in 23 languages, and the Namaste Bharat AI citizen guide with voice and multilingual support.
Assistive and learning solutions:
Divyang Sarthi, a platform with VR-based learning content for persons with intellectual disabilities.
MeitY
reiterated its commitment to regularly updating accessibility guidelines in line with international standards, supporting certification and compliance, building the capacity of officials and developers, and sharing India’s tools and experience. It also said it would continue to develop digital assistive solutions for greater inclusion.

title: Botswana-born Cheetah gives Birth to Four Cubs in the Wild; India’s Cheetah Population Rises to 62
subtitle: Shri Bhupender Yadav acknowledges Dedication, Commitment and Hard Work of Experts and frontline Forest Staff for the Success of Project Cheetah.
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

                20 NOV 2026 10:45AM by PIB Delhi
content:
A two-and-a-half-year-old female cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild today, marking a significant milestone for Project Cheetah and India's efforts towards restoring a viable cheetah population.
In a post on social media, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, stated that KOMG 3 is the first female cheetah from Botswana to give birth. He highlighted that she had spent more than four months in the wild before giving birth under natural conditions. This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.
KOMG 3, a two-and-a-half-year-old female cheetah from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild today. 

Notably, she is the first female cheetah from Botswana to give birth. This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population.

Having spent more than four months in the wild, KOMG 3 has now given birth under natural conditions. This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.

With these four new arrivals, India's cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.

Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort. 

Behind this milestone lie countless hours of dedication, commitment and hard work by the managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
November 20, 2026
Shri Yadav further stated that with the birth of the four cubs, India's cheetah population has increased to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals. He described the development as a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India's journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population.
The Minister noted that every such birth strengthens hope and deepens the commitment towards conservation, while reaffirming that conservation requires patience, perseverance and collective effort. He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

title: Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs foils smuggling attempt of cocaine worth Rs. 5 crore (approx.) at Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 10:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Based on data analysis and intelligence-led surveillance, officers of Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs, foiled an attempt to smuggle cocaine through the Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi.
The consignment, declared as “Beans Cloths” and originating from Entebbe, Uganda, had remained unclaimed for a considerable period after its arrival. No Bill of Entry had been filed for its clearance.
Accordingly, officers of Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs, conducted a detailed examination of the consignment and recovered approximately 1.975 Kg (gross weight) of fabric suspected to be laced with a narcotic substance, along with raw pulses and beans. A separate packet of 350 grams (gross weight) containing white powder suspected to be cocaine was also recovered.
Preliminary testing of the white powder indicated the presence of cocaine. The 1.975 kg impregnated / laced fabric material and 350 grams. packet containing white powdery substance suspected to be cocaine / NDPS substance has been seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
The estimated street value of the seized cocaine is approximately ₹5 crore. It is estimated at ₹10–15 crore per kilogram in the international market. Further investigation is underway.

title: DRI seizes 8 kg methamphetamine (Yaba) tablets in Agartala; one drug trafficker arrested
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 10:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Another successful interdiction by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has resulted in the seizure of
8 kg methamphetamine tablets (Yaba)
in Agartala, Tripura, and the arrest of one drug trafficker. The operation, conducted by DRI on 17 November 2026, marks another significant addition to DRI's sustained efforts to curb the cross-border trafficking of synthetic drugs in the North-Eastern region.
Acting on specific intelligence regarding the movement of a consignment of narcotic drugs, officers of the DRI intercepted the suspected vehicle. When suspected white Maruti Suzuki Swift Dzire was spotted and signalled to stop, its driver attempted to evade interception by speeding away. DRI officers swiftly pursued and intercepted the vehicle near the railway crossing at Iccha Bazar. The occupants abandoned the vehicle and attempted to escape on foot. However, officers managed to apprehend one of them, while the others escaped.
A detailed search of the vehicle led to the recovery of a plastic bag concealed in the footwell of the front passenger seat. The bag contained eight black packets, each holding five white packets, which in turn contained ten pouches of orange-coloured tablets suspected to be methamphetamine.
The recovered 8 kg (net) of methamphetamine tablets, along with the vehicle, was seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. One person was arrested under the provisions of the Act.
This seizure adds to DRI's sustained efforts to interdict substantial consignments of synthetic drugs in the North-Eastern region. Recent operations by DRI in the region have resulted in significant seizures of methamphetamine tablets and crystal methamphetamine, including the seizure of 20 kg Yaba tablets in Silchar last week; 20 kg crystal methamphetamine and 30 kg methamphetamine tablets in two operations during last month in Silchar and Aizawl respectively.
These successive interdictions underscore DRI's intelligence-gathering capabilities and operational vigilance in identifying and disrupting narcotics trafficking networks operating in the region.

Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Shri Chirag Paswan called upon the beverage industry to strengthen India's position as a global hub for manufacturing, innovation and exports while creating greater value from Indian agricultural produce.
Delivering the keynote address at the National Beverage Conclave 2026, organised by the Indian Beverage Association (IBA), Shri Paswan linked the sector's growth to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Sapt Dhara vision, particularly its emphasis on manufacturing, agriculture and food processing, and technology and innovation.

He reaffirmed the Government's commitment to supporting the food processing sector. He also called upon the industry to build consumer trust through scientific evidence, transparent communication and greater consumer awareness, while contributing to India's vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047.
Earlier, IBA President Shri C.K. Jaipuria highlighted the beverage sector's potential to reduce agricultural wastage and support farmers, while calling for stronger industry-government collaboration. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is witnessing encouraging public participation at its Health Pavilion at the 45
th

Visitors, including children, youth, families and other sections of society, are actively participating in the activities being organised across the Pavilion.
Interactive Activities and Cultural Performances Promote Health Awareness
As part of the ongoing public outreach initiatives, Nukkad Natak performances are being organised under the ‘TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan’, alongside awareness activities on vector-borne diseases and filariasis. These performances aim to sensitise visitors about tuberculosis, its symptoms, modes of transmission, prevention, early diagnosis and timely treatment.
Magic shows are also being organised to communicate important health messages through innovative and engaging presentations. Doctors’ talk shows and health awareness sessions provide visitors with opportunities to interact with medical professionals, understand common health concerns and seek guidance on preventive measures and healthy lifestyle practices.
Live Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) demonstrations, interactive quizzes and other stage activities are further familiarising visitors with essential health practices, emergency response techniques and disease prevention. These activities are transforming the Pavilion into an interactive learning space, promoting health awareness through information, demonstration and public participation.
Free Health Screening, Medical Consultations and Counselling Services
Spread across an area of 989 square metres in Hall No. 4(G), Ground Floor, Bharat Mandapam, the Health Pavilion brings together
39 stalls representing 24 National Health Programmes, Programme Divisions and participating organisations
.
Visitors are being provided access to a wide range of healthcare services, basic health screenings, medical consultations, counselling and information, free of cost. These include BMI assessment, blood sugar testing, blood pressure measurement, routine eye check-ups, oral health screening, hearing assessments and blood grouping services.
The Pavilion also provides information on maternal and child healthcare, immunisation, the U-WIN digital vaccination platform and services under the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram. Visitors can access awareness and counselling on HIV/AIDS, sexually transmitted infections, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases, viral hepatitis, leprosy and other public health concerns.
Digital healthcare initiatives, including eSanjeevani teleconsultation services, Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), are also being showcased to familiarise visitors with the availability and benefits of Government healthcare services.
Mental health awareness and counselling services, including information on Tele-MANAS, are being provided alongside specialised services related to eye and vision care, hearing, dental health and organ donation awareness. Visitors are also receiving guidance on nutrition, physical activity, tobacco cessation, food safety and other healthy lifestyle practices.
Representatives of participating organisations and programme divisions are facilitating direct interaction with visitors, helping them understand the healthcare services, benefits and support mechanisms available under various Government initiatives.
Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Healthy Habits Through Play
A dedicated Kids’ Zone has been set up to provide children with opportunities to participate in traditional games and recreational activities. With an emphasis on screen-free engagement, the zone encourages physical activity, social interaction and learning through play. The initiative aims to familiarise children with the importance of healthy habits while offering an engaging and enjoyable experience for families visiting the Pavilion.
The Health Pavilion will continue to host a range of interactive activities, health screening facilities, awareness sessions and public engagement initiatives throughout IITF 2026, which concludes on 27th November 2026.
