The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, celebrated its 12th Convocation Ceremony today at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, addressed the gathering on the occasion in the presence of Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda.
The convocation ceremony marked an important milestone in the academic journey of the graduating students, recognising their dedication, perseverance and commitment to the medical profession.
Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, congratulated the graduating students and appreciated the significant representation of female graduates, observing that the achievements of the daughters reflected the growing participation of women in medical education and the healthcare sector. She highlighted the important role played by Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in providing extensive clinical exposure to medical students. Referring to the hospital's patient footfall, she noted that more than 19 lakh patients availed its OPD services in 2025, providing students with valuable hands-on experience and strengthening their clinical knowledge and confidence.
Highlighting India's transformation in healthcare over the past decade, the President observed that sustained government initiatives had strengthened healthcare delivery from the grassroots to advanced tertiary care. She noted that approximately 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were operational across the country, expanding access to primary healthcare services. She also highlighted the expansion of tertiary healthcare and medical education beyond metropolitan cities into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, enabling people, particularly those from rural and underserved communities, to access specialised healthcare services closer to their homes. She emphasised the importance of telemedicine in bridging geographical barriers and ensuring that quality medical consultations reach people in remote areas.
The President highlighted the shift in India's healthcare approach towards preventive and promotive healthcare, in line with the National Health Policy, 2017. She emphasised the growing importance of early screening, detection and management of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes, mental health conditions and various forms of cancer. She observed that large-scale screening initiatives undertaken across the country were essential to identifying health conditions at an early stage and ensuring timely treatment, particularly among vulnerable populations.
Referring to the Government's initiatives towards strengthening financial protection in healthcare, the President highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), which provides health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year, helping reduce the financial burden of hospitalisation and improving access to quality healthcare for economically vulnerable families. She also highlighted the Ayushman Vaya Vandana Yojana, which extends the benefit of ₹5 lakh health coverage to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.
The President also underscored the importance of integrating traditional systems of medicine with modern healthcare. She noted that efforts to promote Ayurveda and Yoga, alongside modern medical practices, had strengthened the country's holistic approach to health and well-being. She highlighted the co-location of Ayush services in government healthcare institutions and the growing emphasis on collaborative research. She also referred to international cooperation through the Ministry of Ayush and the World Health Organization's Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in advancing research and promoting evidence-based traditional healthcare practices.
Addressing the graduating medical professionals, the President urged them to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics, sensitivity and compassion in their careers. She emphasised that access to quality healthcare must not remain limited to urban centres and privileged sections of society, and called upon the doctors to extend their services to people living in remote and underserved areas. She encouraged the graduates to contribute not only to clinical care but also to medical research, innovation and the development of solutions suited to India's specific socio-economic, nutritional and environmental conditions.
The President further emphasised the transformative potential of emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence, in improving the accessibility, affordability and efficiency of healthcare delivery. Drawing lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, she called upon medical professionals to remain adaptable and embrace technological advancements while ensuring that healthcare remains people-centric.
Emphasising the significance of the One Health approach, the President observed that human health was closely interconnected with animal health, vegetation and the environment. Referring to emerging zoonotic diseases, environmental pollution and climate change, she stressed the need for coordinated efforts among medical professionals, veterinarians, environmental scientists and other stakeholders. She called for greater interdisciplinary collaboration to strengthen disease surveillance, enable early detection and build resilience against future public health challenges.
Addressing the Convocation, Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda, described ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital as a pioneering institution and a beacon of excellence in medical education and healthcare. Furthermore, Shri Nadda appreciated its contributions to medical research, infrastructure development and specialised clinical services.
He highlighted that the institution provides an exceptional learning environment by combining a high volume of patient care with quality medical standards, thereby offering students invaluable clinical exposure and practical experience. He also appreciated the institution's achievements in organ donation, organ retrieval and complex surgical procedures, along with the continuous development of its infrastructure and various departments.
Emphasising that professional medical education is a privilege accompanied by significant social responsibility, the Union Health Minister stated that while primary and secondary education are fundamental rights, medical education is supported by a substantial ecosystem of public investment, institutional resources and societal contributions. Referring to the initiatives undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he highlighted the Government's allocation of ₹15,000 crore towards the creation of 10,000 undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats, underscoring the significant investment made in strengthening India's medical education infrastructure. He urged the graduating doctors to recognise this investment as a responsibility to serve society with dedication, compassion and professional excellence.
Shri Nadda further emphasised that students must remain grateful to their teachers for their guidance and acknowledge the sacrifices and support of their parents throughout their academic journey. He observed that the achievements of medical graduates are not solely the result of their individual efforts but also reflect the collective contribution of families, teachers and the larger society.
Highlighting the transformation of medical education in India over the past decade, the Union Health Minister noted the expansion of the country's healthcare and medical education infrastructure, including the establishment and operationalisation of 23 All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). He observed that these institutions are equipped with modern infrastructure and advanced facilities, strengthening India's capacity to provide quality medical education and specialised healthcare services.
Concluding his address, Shri Nadda reiterated the Government of India's commitment to providing world-class medical education infrastructure and healthcare facilities across the country. He urged the graduating doctors to carry forward the values of professional integrity, compassion and service, and to dedicate their knowledge and skills towards the health and well-being of the nation.
As part of the ceremony, the Union Health Minister released the Annual Report (2025–26) and the ABVIMS Journal, highlighting the institution's academic, clinical, research and institutional achievements.
The convocation formally inducted 324 graduating medical professionals into the healthcare workforce across undergraduate, postgraduate and super-specialty disciplines. The graduating cohort comprised 100 MBBS students from the Batch of 2020, including 79 male and 21 female students. A total of 177 students graduated from MD/MS programmes across 17 broad specialties from the batches of 2022–2025, comprising 115 male and 62 female students. In the super-specialty disciplines, 47 students graduated from DM/M.Ch./DrNB programmes across 13 specialties from the batches of 2022–2025, including 35 male and 12 female students.
A total of 58 Gold Medals were conferred upon top-performing graduates in recognition of their outstanding academic performance and clinical excellence.
Infrastructure and Clinical Milestones
The occasion also highlighted significant advancements in the institution's healthcare infrastructure and clinical capabilities. These included the commissioning of the new 666-bed Super-Specialty Block, featuring dedicated departments for Radiotherapy, Nuclear Medicine, Surgical Oncology and Gastrointestinal Surgery. The new facility has further strengthened the availability of specialised and advanced healthcare services.
Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital also achieved a significant milestone in 2025 by becoming the first Central Government hospital in India to receive full accreditation from the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH), reflecting its commitment to quality healthcare, patient safety and institutional excellence.
The occasion celebrated the achievements of the graduating students and reaffirmed the institution's commitment to excellence in medical education, research and patient care. It also encouraged the next generation of medical professionals to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics, compassion and dedication in their service to the nation.

Assam, Sikkim , Mizoram , Tripura awarded among North-Eastern and Hilly States

Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises
date:

content:
The Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, organised the
SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026
on 20 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The awards were conferred by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, as Guest of Honour, to
recognise the outstanding contributions of States/UTs, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Lending Institutions and partner organisations
in strengthening street vendors’ livelihoods and advancing financial inclusion, digital adoption and social security under the PM SVANidhi Scheme.
Featuring
52 awards and 5 special recognitions
, the awards celebrated excellence across States, cities, banks and other stakeholders. Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh were among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme and expanding its outreach. Cities and ULBs were also recognised for their contribution to effective grassroots implementation, improved outreach and digital adoption.
Among the Lending Institutions,
State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank and Union Bank
were recognised for their lending performance and contribution towards extending accessible formal credit to street vendors.
Since its launch in June 2020, PM SVANidhi has enabled
around 81 lakh street vendors to access over 1.21 crore loans amounting to approximately ₹20,000 crore
. Following the restructuring of the Scheme in August 2025, around 22 lakh loans worth ₹6,294 crore were disbursed to 10.6 lakh new beneficiaries in the first year. The Scheme has also expanded access to formal credit through an UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card, offering eligible beneficiaries who have repaid their second loan tranche a credit limit of up to ₹30,000.
Under
SVANidhi se Samriddhi
, socio-economic profiling of over 52 lakh beneficiary families has been completed, resulting in more than 1.62 crore sanctions under eight Central Government welfare schemes. The Scheme is also strengthening the street vending ecosystem through initiatives such as the development of 50 Street Food Hubs and capacity-building programmes, including food safety and hygiene training.
The awards covered the Scheme's implementation ecosystem across
35 States/UTs, over 4,900 ULBs and more than 120 Lending Institutions
. The assessment was based on category-specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), using data primarily from the PM SVANidhi and SVANidhi se Samriddhi portals. Performance following the Scheme's restructuring was assessed for the period from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026, while overall performance was evaluated from the Scheme's inception up to 31 August 2026.
The SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 recognise the collective contributions of stakeholders towards strengthening the street vending ecosystem and improving the livelihoods of street vendors. These efforts will further promote inclusive urban development and contribute towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
Key Highlights from Addresses
S
hri Manohar Lal emphasised that the vision of
Antyodaya, leading towards Viksit Bharat @2047, can be realised by ensuring that the benefits of PM SVANidhi reach every eligible street vendor. He highlighted that the Scheme enables street vendors to progress from small loans to higher bank credit and expand their businesses, thereby promoting livelihood opportunities, financial inclusion and social security.
The Minister underscored that the success of PM SVANidhi is driven by the collective efforts of the Central and State Governments, banks and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). He noted that the SVANidhi Samman Awards recognise the contributions of States, cities, institutions and officials in translating the objectives of the Scheme into tangible outcomes at the grassroots level.
Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’
, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises.
Referring to the Scheme's song, “Har mehnatkash ka saath diya, PM SVANidhi ne samman diya”
, the Minister highlighted how PM SVANidhi has extended support to hardworking street vendors while strengthening their dignity, recognition and respect in society.
MOS Shri Tokhan Sahu  Speech Highlight
s
Addressing the gathering, Minister of State Shri Tokhan Sahu
emphasised that the transformation in the lives of the poor should be viewed through the collective impact of various Government welfare initiatives rather than through any single scheme. Referring to the World Bank’s October 2026 report, he highlighted that approximately 50 crore people in India have moved out of poverty, reflecting the impact of sustained and coordinated efforts towards inclusive development.
The Minister also highlighted Chhattisgarh’s achievement of receiving four awards, particularly appreciating the recognition of Dantewada and Bade Bacheli, erstwhile Naxal-affected areas. He noted that this achievement reflects the reach of the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the positive transformation taking place in regions progressing towards becoming Naxal-free.

title: Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA chairs 11th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India has sanctioned 1.75 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) and an additional in-principle approval for 1.5 lakh houses was also given during the 11th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) on 19th November 2026.
Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA); Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary and Financial Advisor (JS&FA); Shri Vaibhav Rundwal, Director (HFA), officials from the Ministry; and Mission Directors, representatives from States/UTs were among those present in the meeting.
1.75 lakh houses have been approved in Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0 in States/UTs of Assam (4,841), Goa (06), Gujarat (5,793), Madhya Pradesh (10,913), Maharashtra (19,778), Odisha (2,681), Puducherry (937), Rajasthan (4,572), Tamil Nadu (14,350), Uttar Pradesh (1,01,493) and West Bengal (10,159). Furthermore, in-principle approval has been given for 1,27,349 houses in State of Andhra Pradesh and 22,484 houses in State of Maharashtra, subject to submission of necessary compliance and adherence to Scheme Guidelines by the respective States. This takes the total count of houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 to more than 24.15 lakh. The latest approval marks another significant step towards expanding access to pucca houses for eligible urban families, particularly those belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).
Secretary, DoUD directed States/UTs to accelerate expenditure and ensure optimal utilisation of sanctioned funds, along with ensuring timely release of funds to beneficiaries and implementing agencies for seamless implementation of scheme. He further mentioned about strengthening monitoring, geo-tagging of houses and complete verification of all pending applications within stipulated timelines.
Promoting inclusive and equitable housing, the scheme places women empowerment at its core while also prioritising housing needs of vulnerable sections of society.
A beneficiary family from Gujarat outside their house constructed under PMAY-U 2.0
Meanwhile in the meeting, States/UTs were also advised to formulate comprehensive Affordable Housing Policies and undertake mandatory reforms to create an enabling ecosystem for affordable housing.
PMAY-U 2.0, launched in September 2024, aims to support 1 crore additional eligible EWS/Low Income Group (LIG) and Middle Income Group (MIG) families in constructing or purchasing pucca houses through different verticals. Moreover, the scheme also caters to rental housing needs of urban migrants/working women/urban poor by providing affordable and dignified rental accommodation in cities.
Together under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, 1.29 crore houses have been sanctioned while 1.01 crore houses have been completed.

title: One World, Countless Stories, Infinite Emotions: Goa Rolls Out Red Carpet for IFFI 57
subtitle:
We Want Goa to Be Where Films Are Produced and Completed: CM Pramod Sawant Unveils Goa's Cinematic Vision

Truth, Emotion and a Compelling Story always Connects audience: Ravi Kishan

Cinema is One of India's Most Powerful Expressions of Soft Power: I & B Secretary Chanchal Kumar

A Story Can Cross Borders Without a Passport: Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker

Ricky Kej Strikes a Global Chord as IFFI 2026 Celebrates Music Without Borders
content:
Goa 20 November 2026
Somewhere between the first flash of light and the first frame on screen, the world finds a reason to come together. And today, Goa became that world. Against the shimmering backdrop of the Arabian Sea, Goa once again transformed into a global stage where filmmakers, celebrated screen icons and cinephiles converge, cultures collide and imaginations take flight.
With a spectacular inaugural ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, Goa, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opened its doors to a universe of stories, bringing together 86 nations and over 150 films in a celebration of the limitless magic of the moving image. Inspired by the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, this edition celebrates cinema's extraordinary power to transcend geography, dissolve cultural divides and turn different voices into one shared experience.
Addressing the gathering, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said that IFFI, now an integral part of Goa's cultural calendar for over 22 years, celebrates cinema's power to transcend boundaries and bring cultures together. Linking the festival's theme to India's timeless philosophy of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’—the world is one family, he said, “Cinema allows us to experience different cultures and find the common ground that unites us.”
Describing the inclusion of Ramayana in the BRICS Cinema section as a proud moment for India, he highlighted IFFI's role in showcasing the richness of Indian cinema, particularly Marathi, Konkani and Goan films. He expressed hope that this recognition would inspire more young Goans to pursue filmmaking and take their stories to national and international audiences.
Outlining Goa's vision of becoming a comprehensive filmmaking hub, Dr. Sawant said, “We want Goa to be the destination where films are produced and completed.” He highlighted the Goa Film Shooting Act, 2021, the online single-window clearance system and financial assistance schemes for filmmakers as key initiatives to strengthen the state's film ecosystem. He also announced the vision of a film city equipped with pre-production, post-production, VFX and film education facilities.
Emphasising the opportunities emerging from technological advancements in animation, artificial intelligence and virtual production, he said Goa aims to equip its young creative talent to be part of the evolving global film industry.
Speaking on the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, noted actor and Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan said that the theme resonated deeply with him, given his experience of working in nearly 700 films across different Indian languages and regions. He observed that audiences, irrespective of language or geography, connect with the same essential elements of cinema—truth, emotion and a compelling story.
“A story born in one corner of the world can find a home thousands of miles away. That is the magic of cinema,” he said, highlighting its power to transcend boundaries and create shared human experiences. He also acknowledged the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in strengthening India's vibrant film industry, noting that India is the world's largest film-producing nation.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, highlighted cinema's power to transcend borders and unite diverse cultures and perspectives. Describing IFFI as more than a celebration of films, he said, “It is a meeting place of cultures, ideas, memories and human experiences.”
Quoting the Rig Vedic thought,
“Let noble thoughts come to us from all directions,”
he emphasised that openness to the world enriches India's identity. Calling cinema one of India's most powerful expressions of soft power, he noted that this spirit of cultural exchange is reflected in IFFI 2026 through special showcases from Russia and Spain and 21 films from BRICS nations.
Reflecting on this year's theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, he said, “A story from one part of the world can enter another through emotion, imagination and human experience.” He also highlighted IFFI's commitment to fresh voices and inclusive storytelling, with 52 women filmmakers and 62 debut filmmakers featuring in this year's festival.
Setting the context for this year’s festival, IFFI Festival Director, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker reflected on the unifying power of cinema in a paradoxical era where hyper-connectivity often leads to cultural isolation. Articulating the philosophy behind this year’s festival theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, he reminded the audience that division is often self-imposed. "Borders are not merely lines drawn on maps. They are also our habits we build around ourselves”, he flagged.
Highlighting how cinema dissolves these barriers, Gowariker observed that when viewers empathize with characters in an unfamiliar language, the distance between people immediately shrinks. "A story is one of the few things that can cross these borders without a passport," he remarked. To bring this vision to life, this edition of IFFI showcases an expansive slate of nine World Premieres, two International Premieres, 24 Asian Premieres, and 116 Indian Premieres, serving as an open invitation to transcend boundaries between nations, cinematic eras, emerging voices, and the vibrant host city itself.
The opening ceremony was graced by Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) Shri Sadanand Mhalu Shet Tanavade; Member of Legislative Assembly from Siolim and Vice Chairperson of the Entertainment Society of Goa Smt. Delilah Lobo; Chief Secretary of Goa Dr. V. Candavelou; Chairman, National Film Development Corporation of India Shri G. Krishnakumar; Chairman, Prasar Bharati Shri Prasoon Joshi; Managing Director, National Film Development Corporation Shri Dhiraj Singh; and Chief Executive Officer, Entertainment Society of Goa Shri Dipak Bandekar.
Film personalities including Kartik Aaryan and Sai Pallavi added star power to the opening ceremony.
International Competition Jury Chairman Mr Aanand L. Rai along with jury members  Mr. Bogdan Mureșanu, Ms. Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière, Ms. María Alejandra Rojas, Mr. Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke were felicitated in the opening ceremony. Chairperson of Indian Panorama Feature section Shri Madhur Bhandarkar and Chairperson of Non-Feature film section Shri Himanshu Sekhar Khatua were also felicitated.
Global musical performances add to the opening spectacle
The opening ceremony featured a series of musical and cultural performances celebrating the universal language of cinema. The symphonic orchestra led by three-time Grammy Award-winning composer Ricky Kej on the theme ‘A World of Cinema Through Music’ took audiences on a musical journey across cultures and storytelling traditions, highlighting cinema’s ability to transcend linguistic and geographical boundaries.
The inaugural night also featured ‘Music Without Borders’, an international musical collaboration involving musicians from different countries to celebrate musical traditions, harmony and cultural exchange. The festival’s iconic peacock motif was featured in ‘Beyond the Frame’, a special dance presentation that brought the IFFI emblem to life through movement and artistic expression.
WAVES Film Bazaar Celebrates 20 Glorious Years
Celebrating two decades of connecting Indian cinema with global opportunities, the 20th WAVES Film Bazaar opened in Goa on November 20, 2026, alongside the 57th IFFI. A special audio-visual presentation at the inaugural ceremony showcased its remarkable journey and contribution to film business, co-production, financing, networking and global collaborations. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), WAVES Film Bazaar has grown from 204 delegates across 18 countries in 2007 to a premier international marketplace, bringing together over 2,500 film professionals from more than 40 countries.
Highlights of IFFI-2026
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) promises a spectacular celebration of cinema, bringing together over 150 films from 86 countries under the inspiring theme,
‘Stories Without Borders’.
Selected from more than 1,900 submissions representing 137 countries, the festival presents a compelling cinematic journey, with
Fatherland
as the opening film,
I Matter
as the mid-festival film, and
We Are All Strangers
as the closing film.
Adding new dimensions to the cinematic experience, this year’s festival introduces two exciting sections—
Animation
and
Films About Films
. Spain takes centre stage as the Country of Honour, Russia joins as the Partner Country, while the
BRICS Cinema
showcase celebrates the diverse cinematic voices of emerging global narratives. The Indian Panorama further captures the richness of the country's storytelling traditions, featuring
76 films across 18 languages
.
With a strong commitment to nurturing fresh talent and promoting inclusivity, IFFI 2026 shines a spotlight on
52 women filmmakers and 62 debut directors
. The sixth edition of
Creative Minds of Tomorrow
will provide mentorship to 100 young filmmakers across 13 crafts, empowering the next generation of creative voices. Complementing this initiative, 14 masterclasses and panel discussions will create a vibrant platform for learning, collaboration, dialogue and creative exchange.
More than a celebration of films, IFFI 2026 is a confluence of cultures, perspectives and creative voices, reaffirming the power of cinema to transcend borders and bring the world together. Cinema, after all, speaks a language without borders, spins stories without boundaries and sets emotions in motion. As nine days of cinematic discovery unfold, one thing is certain: the world may be divided by borders, but in the dark of a cinema hall, we all dream in the same light.

title: From Ancestral Roots to Human Bonds, 12 Goan Films Bring Local Stories to the Global Stage at 57th IFFI
subtitle: Films in Konkani and Marathi explore identity, family, social realities and the complexities of everyday life
content:
Goa, 20 November 2026
Long celebrated across the world for its coastal charm, vibrant heritage, and unmatched hospitality, Goa has another side that deserves equal attention — its stories and the people behind them. At the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), a specially curated package brings this side of Goa to the screen, exploring lives, relationships, memories and experiences that are both deeply local and universally relatable.
Scheduled for screening from November 21 to 28 at INOX Panjim, this collection of films traverses a rich emotional landscape. Stories of an elderly woman confronting her conscience, a forgotten local hero whose past resurfaces, a daughter seeking reconciliation with her family, and an elderly villager defending his ancestral home reflect the range of human experiences explored through these films.
Spanning Konkani and Marathi, the selection comprises feature and short films that explore a wide spectrum of themes, including family relationships, social realities, personal struggles, identity, childhood, loneliness and personal discovery. From deeply personal narratives to quirky comedies and thought-provoking dramas, the films offer audiences an engaging glimpse into the evolving landscape of filmmaking in Goa.
A glimpse into the Goan film selection:
ANCESSAO
Director: Manguirish J. Bandodkar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 30 minutes
Set in a quiet Goan village,
Ancessao
follows an elderly woman living alone, filling the silence of her life with conversations about others. Unable to confront her own grief, she eventually recognises her gossip as a distraction from an unhealed wound. When her conscience prompts her to change, she makes a resolve to mend her ways, but the transformation proves short-lived.
UMESH
Director: Vardhan Vijaykumar Kamat | Language: Konkani | Duration: 1 hour 39 minutes
Once a celebrated local hero, Umesh now leads a reclusive life in a rural Goan village, surviving on odd jobs and haunted by an unresolved past. His life takes an unexpected turn when aspiring filmmakers Anton and Rohan arrive to document him. As they navigate local rumours and half-truths, they uncover a forgotten talent and the painful circumstances behind his isolation. As trust gradually develops, Umesh grows increasingly wary of the camera.
Umesh
explores identity, trust and the cost of a forgotten legacy.
SHAKUNTALA
Director: Prasad M. Naik | Language: Konkani | Duration: 11 minutes
An emotional family drama about love, identity and tradition,
Shakuntala
follows a woman estranged from her conservative family after marrying a Christian man from her neighbourhood. Years later, following her father's death, she is denied the opportunity to attend his funeral. As the twelfth-day death ritual approaches, Shakuntala gathers the courage to return to her childhood home, confronting buried conflicts and societal judgment. Her journey is not merely to fulfil a ritual but to reclaim her place as a daughter and question whether love can transcend tradition.
PURNATA
Director: Shravan Kankonkar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 25 minutes
Through the journey of Zayo, a garland of jasmine flowers,
Purnata
captures the many lives it touches, bringing comfort, hope and joy through moments of happiness and sadness. Even as the flowers gradually wither, they continue to make lives beautiful. The film reflects on the continuity of life and purpose, suggesting that even when one life ends, another carries the journey forward.
NOISE
Director: Suvidha Torgal Bakhle | Language: Konkani | Duration: 16 minutes
An intimate exploration of human behaviour and relationships,
Noise
follows Tara as she struggles to break free from a troubled relationship and recurring patterns that cause her distress. Despite her efforts to heal and move forward, she repeatedly finds herself drawn towards the familiar. The recurring presence of an old fan becomes a metaphor for these cycles of behaviour, echoing the film's central reflection on the difficulty of changing even when one recognises the need to do so.
DARYAA
Director: Kishor Arjun | Language: Marathi | Duration: 25 minutes
Daryaa
tells the story of Aakash, a visually impaired boy with cerebral palsy who has never seen the sea and knows it only through stories, sounds and imagination. When his grandfather takes him on an unexpected journey to the coast, Aakash encounters the world he has long dreamed of. The film explores the profound experience of discovering the sea and reminds us that seeing may have little to do with sight.
PERFECT SHOT
Director: Sankalp Sainath Parab | Language: Konkani | Duration: 14 minutes
For Vasudha, a young film school student, the quest for the perfect cinematic frame becomes an obsession shaped by the Golden Ratio, symmetry and the rule of thirds. At the same time, she struggles with unresolved emotions towards her late father, believing he left her with nothing of value. As memories resurface, her pursuit of visual perfection turns into a personal journey of discovery. The film explores how relationships shape our vision and creativity, revealing that meaningful storytelling goes beyond the technical rules of cinema.
BAPO KALE
Director: Krisha Raul | Language: Konkani | Duration: 24 minutes
Set in the village of Mauxi,
Bapo Kale
follows an elderly man who refuses to leave his ancestral mud house when an emergency evacuation drill reaches his doorstep. What begins as a routine exercise brings back memories of displacement, lost homes and a changing village. As Bapo and his wife Bhagi confront the authorities through a tense night, their home emerges as a powerful symbol of identity, dignity, memory and an enduring connection to the land.
WOODWORM (ROTO)
Director: Akhil Lotlikar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 22 minutes
Woodworm (Roto)
follows a determined clinic receptionist navigating a chaotic family situation as she tries to help her sister win a school competition. But as she struggles to balance family responsibilities and her sister's aspirations, an unforeseen danger begins to close in on her.
CHEERS!
Director: Anurag Verdekar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 19 minutes
Bored with their routine, two young boys board a random bus and embark on an aimless journey into the unfamiliar world of adults. Their adventure takes them to an old fort, across a river ferry and eventually to a secluded waterfall, where they impulsively decide to buy their first alcoholic drink. Their unsuccessful attempt to conceal their age exposes their vulnerability and brings home the realisation that the adult world is far more complicated than they imagined.
Cheers!
captures the curiosity, innocence and uncertainties of growing up, as the boys return home with a subtly changed perspective on the world.
MEDIUM PIECE
Director: Jay Amonkar | Language: Marathi | Duration: 23 minutes
A chicken escaping from a butcher's shop sets off an unusual chain of events in this bittersweet comedy-drama set in a rural village. Blamed for repeatedly losing chickens, the butcher comes up with an unconventional solution: installing a television to keep the birds entertained. However, he soon becomes addicted to the television himself, affecting his behaviour, responsibilities and relationship with his wife. When the television malfunctions and all the chickens escape, the butcher faces punishment from his employer and rejection at home. Through this quirky tale of a man caught between captivity and the desire for escape,
Medium Piece
explores loneliness, modern distractions and the unintended consequences of seeking an escape from everyday life.
HEALTH CENTRE
Director: Anup Sardesai | Language: Konkani | Duration: 2 hours 7 minutes
Set in a chaotic government health centre,
Health Centre
follows Dr. Sridhar Kamat, its Chief Medical Officer, as he confronts a moral crisis involving a young rape victim, Surbhi, who is pressured by corrupt politicians and police to withdraw her complaint against an influential accused, Ajay. Amid a workers' strike, he also struggles to provide care for a comatose patient whose daughter, Manisha, depends on the hospital's limited resources. When Surbhi finally succumbs to intimidation, Dr. Kamat takes justice into his own hands by secretly administering a fatal injection to Ajay before resigning in protest, while ensuring the comatose patient remains on life support. Ten years later, his legacy resurfaces when his son Raj joins a new facility and encounters a senior doctor who is revealed to be Surbhi.
Goa has been the permanent home of the International Film Festival of India since 2004, welcoming filmmakers, cinema enthusiasts and creative voices from across the world every November. The 57th edition, being held from November 20 to 28, 2026, under the theme
‘Stories Without Borders’
, celebrates cinema's ability to transcend geographical, linguistic and cultural boundaries, connecting audiences through shared human experiences.
The Goan film selection is a fitting reflection of this spirit. Rooted in the everyday lives, cultural traditions and social realities of Goa, these twelve films demonstrate how stories that emerge from a particular place can speak to audiences far beyond it.
Whether exploring family relationships, questions of identity, childhood, loneliness or the complexities of social life, they offer perspectives shaped by local experiences but connected by universal emotions.
By bringing Konkani and Marathi cinema to an international platform, the 57th edition of IFFI creates an opportunity for these voices to travel beyond their immediate cultural and linguistic contexts, allowing audiences from across the world to discover Goa not just as a destination, but through the lives, memories and stories of its people. In the spirit of the theme of this year’s festival ‘Stories Without Borders’, the selection reminds us that while stories may begin locally, their ability to move, connect and resonate knows no boundaries.

title: India premiere of Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland opens 57th IFFI, taking audiences through a divided post-war Germany
subtitle:
Fatherland reflects IFFI’s slogan of ‘stories without borders’: Producer Ewa Puszczyńska

Culture the strongest foundation of India-Poland friendship: Piotr Antoni Świtalski
content:
Goa, 20 November 2026
A journey through a nation scarred by war, divided by ideology and grappling with the weight of its past marked the opening of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. Acclaimed filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski’s
Fatherland
(
Ojczyzna
) opened the nine-day festival with its India Premiere, offering audiences an evocative portrait of post-war Germany at the dawn of the Cold War.
The black-and-white drama, directed by the Oscar-winning filmmaker, weaves together history, family relationships and the complexities of a divided homeland through the story of Nobel Prize-winning German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika. The film drew a full house across all screening halls of INOX, setting an impressive note for the opening of the nine-day festival.
Before the screening, Ms. Ewa Puszczyńska, Producer,
Fatherland
, Mr. Piotr Antoni Świtalski, Head of Mission, Poland Embassy, New Delhi and Ms. Małgorzata Wejsis-Gołębiak,  Director, Polish Institute in New Delhi walked the red carpet at INOX, Panjim.
Speaking about the film, Ms. Ewa Puszczyńska highlighted how it’s very making embodied the spirit of IFFI's theme. She said that although
Fatherland
tells the story of a German writer and the German people in the German language, it was made entirely with Polish hearts and hands. This, she said, reflected the festival's slogan of stories without borders.
Mr. Piotr Antoni Świtalski said that while friendship between India and Poland was growing across multiple dimensions, culture remained its strongest foundation. He added that Paweł Pawlikowski brought a fresh focus and perspective to the traditional Polish school of filmmaking.
Felicitating the guests, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said that
Fatherland
offered a special opportunity to celebrate the creative relationship between Poland and India. Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, IFFI, Shri G. Krishnakumar, Chairman, National Film Development Corporation of India and Shri Pankaj Saxena, Artistic Director, IFFI were also present.
A father-daughter journey through a fractured Germany
Set in the summer of 1949, against the backdrop of the emerging Cold War,
Fatherland
follows Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika as they return to Germany after sixteen years of exile in the United States. Travelling in a black Buick across a country still bearing the devastation of the Second World War, the father-daughter duo journey from US-administered Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.
For Mann, the return is far more than a homecoming. It is an encounter with a homeland transformed by war and fractured by competing political ideologies. As the journey unfolds, the divisions of the country find echoes in the complexities of the Mann family, bringing questions of belonging, identity, memory and reconciliation into sharp focus.
Featuring Sandra Hüller and Hanns Zischler in the lead roles, the 82-minute film is a co-production of Poland, Germany, Italy and France. It has featured at major international film festivals, including Cannes, San Sebastián and Telluride this year. Pawlikowski received the Best Director Award at the Cannes Film Festival for the film.

title: ‘Stories Without Borders’: IFFI 57 to celebrate cinema beyond geographical and socio-cultural boundaries
subtitle: Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker outlines vision for the 57th edition; urges media to explore diverse cinematic sections and showcase the festival’s global appeal
content:
Goa, 20 November 2026
A media briefing was held today at the PIB Media Centre, Panaji, Goa on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).
The session brought together
Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, IFFI 57, and Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC). It was moderated by Smt. Smita Vats Sharma, Director General (West), Press Information Bureau (PIB).
Addressing the media, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker outlined his vision for the 57th edition of IFFI, centred on the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’. He explained that the theme extends beyond geographical and territorial boundaries to explore divisions within families and societies, including those arising from caste, social differences and other socio-cultural realities. The festival seeks to bring together stories that transcend such boundaries and reflect shared human experiences across cultures.
Highlighting the festival's diverse cinematic offerings, Shri Gowariker announced the introduction of three new sections this year i.e. Animation, Documentary and Films about Films. He underscored the growing significance of documentaries and the need to provide greater visibility and opportunities to documentary filmmakers. As part of this initiative, IFFI will host a special gala presentation featuring films by winners of the recently concluded Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF).
Emphasising the significance of the festival's varied programming, he noted that every section, including retrospectives, curated showcases and special screenings, contributes to presenting the richness and diversity of cinema. He encouraged media professionals to explore the festival beyond their individual film preferences and attend gala screenings, red-carpet events, international press conferences and Panorama interactions. Such engagements, he observed, offer filmmakers and visiting delegates an opportunity to present their work while enabling audiences to discover diverse cinematic perspectives.
Underscoring the role of media in amplifying the festival's reach, Shri Gowariker urged media representatives to watch and cover films across different sections, including retrospectives, while retaining their independent judgement and critical perspectives. He emphasised that media engagement plays an important role in taking the stories and cinematic offerings of IFFI to audiences across the country.
He also expressed his willingness to facilitate meaningful and informal interactions between the festival team and media representatives throughout the event. Noting the professional commitments of media personnel, he said that the scheduling of interactions had been adjusted to provide greater flexibility and adequate time for coverage of festival activities.
During the briefing, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker also unveiled the official brochure of the 57th International Film Festival of India.
The media interaction provided an overview of the festival's vision and programming priorities, while highlighting the importance of media engagement and collective efforts in strengthening IFFI as an international platform for cinema and cross-cultural exchange.

title: From Creative Ideas to Global Opportunities: WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 Begins in Goa
subtitle: Two decades of connecting filmmakers, nurturing stories and fostering international partnerships
content:
Goa, 20 November 2026
The 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar was inaugurated today at Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon, Goa, marking two decades of fostering connections between Indian and international film industries. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), under the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, the five-day marketplace brings together filmmakers, producers, writers, investors, distributors and other industry professionals to explore collaborations and take creative projects towards global markets.
In the keynote address during the inauguration, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, highlighted the remarkable growth of Film Bazaar from 204 delegates representing 18 countries in 2007 to more than 2,500 delegates in recent editions. He described WAVES Film Bazaar as a platform that transforms creative conception into commercial opportunities.
Referring to the vision of ‘Create in India, Create for the World’, articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at WAVES 2025, he emphasised the importance of providing Indian creative talent with greater access to international markets and opportunities. He described Film Bazaar as a platform for collaboration and discovery, inviting filmmakers from across the world to make full use of the marketplace, where stories can evolve into partnerships and creativity can generate enduring economic and cultural value.
Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Addressing the gathering as Guest of Honour, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director highlighted the unique role of Film Bazaar in bringing Indian filmmakers and international industry professionals together.
Emphasising that the platform engages with filmmakers at every stage of their creative journey, he said WAVES Film Bazaar does not wait for a film to be completed but meets filmmakers wherever they are in the process. Whether a filmmaker has an unfinished script or a completed film seeking an audience, the marketplace brings together people who can help take the project forward. He described how a simple conversation, often beginning with an invitation to have coffee, could open doors to meaningful collaborations.
Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director
Highlighting the transformative power of cinema, he observed that enabling people to see things differently was a gift. He urged delegates to make the most of the four days, interact with strangers, share their ideas, particularly unfinished projects, and pursue opportunities with the hope of finding a ‘yes’.
Welcoming the gathering, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director NFDC described Film Bazaar as an integral part of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI), noting that the platform had maintained this association over the past two decades. He observed that Film Bazaar had grown into a much bigger and wider platform, expanding its scope and opportunities for the film industry.
From right- Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, MIB, G Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, MIB, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director NFDC
Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, delivered the vote of thanks. The inaugural ceremony was also attended by G Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC.
As WAVES Film Bazaar marks two decades, its role extends beyond bringing the film industry together to creating possibilities for stories to travel further. By connecting filmmakers with producers, writers, investors and distributors from across the world, the marketplace seeks to ensure that promising ideas find the right collaborators and that diverse Indian stories have opportunities to reach international audiences. The emphasis remains on creating a space where conversations lead to collaborations and creative possibilities find their way to the screen.

title: NFDC Partners with Svayam to Make 57th IFFI Accessible and Inclusive for All
subtitle:
Collaboration to focus on accessibility audits of festival venues, sensitisation of volunteers and an interactive simulation zone to promote an inclusive cinematic experience

Initiative aims to set a benchmark for accessibility and inclusion at cultural events
content:
Goa, 20 November 2026
The National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) has partnered with Svayam to make the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) more accessible and inclusive for all cine-goers, including persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility. This marks the third collaboration between the two organisations, following their partnerships at the 55th IFFI and the 18th Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF).
As the Accessibility Partner, Svayam is undertaking accessibility audits across festival venues to identify potential barriers and recommend measures to ensure safer, more comfortable and independent access for visitors.
The partnership also includes sensitisation workshops for festival volunteers on disability and accessibility. The sessions will focus on respectful communication, inclusive assistance and practical ways to support persons with diverse accessibility needs.
An
Accessibility Simulation Zone
will further provide visitors and festival stakeholders with an interactive opportunity to understand the everyday barriers faced by persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility. The initiative aims to foster greater awareness, empathy and understanding of the importance of accessible public spaces.
Speaking about the partnership, Ms. Sminu Jindal, Managing Director, Svayam, said, “Accessibility is not merely about creating ramps or making physical spaces barrier-free; it is about ensuring that every individual has the dignity, independence and opportunity to participate equally in society. Cinema is a powerful medium that brings people together, transcends boundaries and celebrates diverse human experiences. It is therefore essential that film festivals are equally welcoming and accessible to everyone. Our collaboration with NFDC for the 57th IFFI is an important step towards making inclusion an integral part of the festival experience. We envision an IFFI where reduced mobility, whether due to age, temporary injury or permanent disability, does not become a barrier to experiencing the joy of cinema.”
Emphasising the importance of the initiative, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC, said, “The International Film Festival of India celebrates the universal language of cinema, and it is important that this celebration is truly open to everyone. Our partnership with Svayam is a significant step towards making the 57th IFFI more accessible, inclusive and welcoming for all cine-goers. Through accessible venues and trained and sensitised volunteers, we aim to create an environment where everyone can participate in the festival with dignity, comfort and independence. We hope this initiative will set a meaningful benchmark for inclusive cultural and cinematic events in India.”
The collaboration marks another step towards making India's premier film festival a truly inclusive celebration of cinema, ensuring that persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility can participate, connect and experience the power of storytelling with dignity and independence.

title: Ministry of Jal Shakti launches ‘Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya’ (SSGB) campaign on World Toilet Day 2026
subtitle:
Nationwide campaign to run from 19th November to 10th December 2026, culminating on Human Rights Day

Campaign to focus on assessments and improvements by States/UTs of functionality and accessibility of community and institutional toilets in rural areas
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 9:01AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, launched the
‘Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya’ (SSGB) campaign
under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)] yesterday on World Toilet Day, 2026. The campaign and its reporting module were e-launched by Ms. Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary & National Mission Director, SBM(G), DDWS.
The event commenced with welcome remarks and context setting for the campaign by the Deputy Secretary, DDWS. This was followed by a brief presentation on the progress of SBM(G) by Director, DDWS which highlighted the achievement of ODF Plus (Model) status in around 89.9% villages and achievements under other components of SBM(G).
Thereafter the ‘
Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya
’ campaign was e-launched by Joint Secretary & National Mission Director. She also launched the reporting module designed by DDWS for States/UTs to report progress of the campaign.
The United Nations theme for World Toilet Day 2026, ‘
Safe toilets. Equal futures
.’, links sanitation to gender equality. Aligned with the same, the
Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya
campaign focuses on improving rural sanitation facilities, with particular attention to the needs of women, girl students and
Divyangjan
.
The objectives of
Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya
campaign include: -
Assessment of the status of CSCs and institutional toilets
(Schools, Anganwadi centres and Panchayat Ghar etc) and undertake repairs/maintenance/restoration, as required. For institutional toilets this may be done through concerned authorities (SMC/AWC/GPK/GPB etc). Motivating individual households to also undertake repair/maintenance of their IHHLs, where warranted.
Assessment of toilet typology for the village and retrofitting
of identified single-pit toilets to twin-pit toilets and septic tank without soak pits to septic tank with soak pits, wherever feasible, against targets set by States/UTs.
Assessment and planning of mechanized desludging
wherever operational or required for FSM compliance.
Assessment and strengthening of O&M arrangements
for the upkeep and maintenance of CSCs and institutional toilets.
Encourage communities to transform
CSCs and institutional toilets into welcoming, clean and well-maintained spaces
with local wall art, signage and improvement of surroundings. Individual households may also be motivated to do the same for their IHHLs.
Assessment of the ODF sustainability in the village; promote continued use of toilets through intensive Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) and awareness drives to sustain ODF status.
Assess the status of Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) for the village(s)/Gram Panchayat
and ensure SSA completion by 30th November 2026, if not done already; Where SSA has been submitted, way forward for resolution of identified gaps to be discussed.
Awareness generation
on various aspects including, importance of sanitation with particular attention to the needs of women, girl students and Divyangjan/PwDs, maintenance of personal and community hygiene, hand washing with soap, importance of FSM compliance, compliance of Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, 4-way segregation of waste and Swachh Seva Aankalan.
Following this, States/UTs participated in an interaction and apprised regarding their proposed action plans for campaign implementation. SBM(G) teams from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Sikkim and Karnataka shared their planned activities for the campaign.
Speaking at the e-launch, Ms. Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary & National Mission Director, SBM(G), emphasised that the
Swachh Shauchalay – Garimamay Bhavishya
campaign has been designed around dignity for all and sanitation for all. She highlighted that the SSGB campaign also focuses on school children as future custodians of
Swachhata,
sensitizing them on
Swachhata, importance of sanitation & hygiene and community participation for keeping toilets clean and accessible to all.
Joint Secretary & National Mission Director, SBM(G) called on the State/UT SBM(G) teams to coordinate with School Management Committees and the concerned Departments to facilitate participation of school children in the campaign including for school sanitation audits. She further highlighted the importance of clean and functional CSCs at places with high public footfall areas including in tourist places in the country, recognizing their contribution directly to overall visitor experience and indirectly to the local economy.
The e- launch concluded with an appeal to all States/UTs for ensuring engagement with different stakeholders, making it a successful campaign driven by
Jan Bhagidari
for
Sampoorna Swachhata
.

title: India's Critical Mineral Push is Securing Mineral Supplies through both Domestic and Overseas Sources: Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Speaking at the Ministry of Mines-FICCI closed-door industry interaction
Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Government of India
, highlighted the Ministry's reform agenda to enhance the sector's global competitiveness through geological exploration, responsible mining, advanced processing, research, recycling and technology-enabled governance. He also outlined recent auction reforms, including relaxation of minimum bidder requirements for certain minerals and automatic issuance of Letters of Intent.
Responding comprehensively to the concerns raised by the industry, Shri Chandra apprised participants of the various initiatives and measures already undertaken or under consideration by the Ministry. He addressed operational challenges relating to mineral block development. He urged the industry to actively consider extraction of critical minerals from resources such as redmud.
The interaction also witnessed the launch of concept paper,
Enabling Overseas Investment in Critical Minerals: Policy, Financial and Institutional Framework for Securing India's Critical Mineral Supply Chains
. Shri Chandra emphasised that to secure mineral supplies, opportunities are being explored both at domestic as well as overseas level. He observed that the paper's emphasis on moving from MoUs to project delivery aligns with the Ministry's efforts, including KABIL's overseas engagements, and expressed interest in examining its recommendations.
On overseas critical mineral investments, he discussed the importance of enabling mechanisms to improve project viability. He emphasised the Ministry's continued efforts to address industry concerns through policy and regulatory reforms, institutional coordination and targeted interventions, while encouraging industry to actively participate in strengthening India's domestic and overseas mineral supply chains.
Opening the interaction, Dr. Pankaj Satija, Co-Chair, FICCI Mining Committee and Executive VP, JSW, appreciated the Ministry's reforms in exploration, mineral auctions and mine operationalisation. He highlighted growing global supply chain vulnerabilities arising from export controls, domestic value-addition requirements and processing technology restrictions, underscoring the importance of diversified and resilient mineral supply chains for India's industrial and economic security.
FICCI noted that the concept paper, prepared pursuant to the mandate received from the Ministry of Mines, draws on extensive research and stakeholder consultations to identify barriers to overseas mineral investments and propose actionable solutions.
The paper also presents a Country-Priority Mineral Matrix to guide strategic overseas investments and proposes a tiered framework for prioritising projects for government facilitation. It emphasises stronger institutional coordination, streamlined approvals and integration of overseas mineral investments with domestic processing and manufacturing capabilities to translate international partnerships into assured mineral supplies for India.
Under the guidance of Shri Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Head, National Critical Mineral Mission, Ministry of Mines, the paper has been authored by Mr. Arpan Gupta, Director, FICCI and Mr. Siddhant Chandra, Assistant Director, FICCI.

Professor Shekhar C. Mande, President of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), has been appointed by the United Nations Secretary-General to the
United Nations Group of Ten High-level Representatives of Civil Society, Private Sector and Scientific Community to Promote Science, Technology and Innovation for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
for the 2026–2028 term.
Professor Mande joins nine other eminent experts from across the world in the High-Level Expert Group, which includes Ms. Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana) and Mr. Giorgio Rossi (Italy) as Co-Chairs, along with Mr. Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Ms. Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Ms. Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russian Federation), Ms. Motoko Kotani (Japan), Mr. Jin Li (China), Mr. Madin Maseeh (Maldives), and Ms. Rita Orji (Nigeria). The Group works closely with the UN Inter-agency Task Team on Science, Technology and Innovation for the SDGs (IATT), providing guidance and recommendations on emerging scientific and technological developments and their implications for sustainable development.
The Group's mandate includes contributing to the UN Science, Technology and Innovation Forum, providing recommendations on technology solutions and partnerships, and advising on areas such as emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, digitalisation, biotechnology, quantum technologies, capacity building, social inclusion and STI roadmaps for the SDGs.
Professor Mande is a distinguished structural and computational biologist and scientific administrator. He is currently President of INSA and a Distinguished Professor at the Bioinformatics Centre, Savitribai Phule Pune University, as well as a JC Bose Fellow at the National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune. Professor Mande also serves as the National President of Vijnana Bharati, a national science movement dedicated to promoting scientific awareness in India. He has previously served as Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Government of India.

title: India Emerging as a Global Research Hub for Diabetes, Genetic Disorders and Next-Generation Healthcare Solutions: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:

content:
India is emerging as a global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders and next-generation healthcare solutions, with over a dozen diabetes-related research projects currently underway under the Ministry of Science & Technology, largely through the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and some through CSIR, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today.
Emphasising that research is increasingly focused on the prevention and control of diabetes through next-generation molecular and genetic solutions, Dr. Singh said India’s vast population and genetic diversity offer a unique opportunity to develop scientific insights and healthcare solutions with relevance for the country and the world. He cautioned that preventing obesity and diabetes among India’s youth is a national responsibility and not merely a medical challenge, requiring collective action beyond the healthcare fraternity.
Dr. Jitendra Singh was addressing the inaugural ceremony of RSSDI 2026, being held from November 19–22 at Bengaluru. The conference brings together leading diabetologists, clinicians, researchers, academicians and healthcare professionals from across the country and abroad. Among the prominent dignitaries present were Shri Krishna Byre Gowda, Hon’ble Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development and Parliamentary Affairs, Government of Karnataka; Dr. C. N. Manjunath, Member of Parliament. The inaugural programme also featured fellowship distribution, recognition of awardees and the launch of books and guidelines.
The Minister said India has undergone a significant transformation in its scientific and healthcare capabilities, moving from dependence on external solutions to developing indigenous vaccines, therapies, antibiotics and advanced medical technologies. Referring to India’s DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, indigenous antibiotics, genetic therapy research, biosimilars and the India Genome Study, he said the country has emerged as a frontline contributor to scientific research, with its research ecosystem increasingly addressing complex health challenges through innovative approaches. He also referred to India’s vaccine pipeline for diseases such as HPV, dengue and malaria, and advances in genetic therapies, demonstrating the expanding scope of Indian biomedical research.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the growing focus on precision medicine and molecular-level interventions is opening new avenues for understanding Type 2 diabetes, associated metabolic disorders and their prevention, particularly among younger populations. He invited greater collaboration between government research institutions, private-sector researchers, clinicians, startups and medical associations, stating that translational research and public-private partnerships are essential to convert scientific discoveries into practical healthcare solutions.
Among the major research initiatives underway is an Indo-Danish collaborative study examining India-specific changes in gut microbiota among prediabetic and diabetic patients, aimed at advancing understanding of the role of gut microbial patterns in metabolic disorders. Another DBT-supported study involves genetically engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 capable of producing GLP-1, with the potential to be developed as a probiotic-based approach for delivering therapeutic molecules through the gastrointestinal tract, with human studies expected to be undertaken. Research at BRIC-THSTI is also exploring the expression of GLP-1 analogues in gut-associated bacteria to investigate new approaches for delivering GLP-1-based therapies.
The Minister also referred to research exploring preconception-to-early-childhood interventions to reduce cardiometabolic risks, including childhood blood glucose, blood pressure and adiposity, as well as the EINSTEIN study being undertaken in rural Mysuru. These initiatives, he said, could generate evidence for strengthening preventive healthcare strategies and addressing metabolic risks from early stages of life. He also referred to research examining the intergenerational impact of nutrition during pregnancy on the metabolic health of offspring.
Highlighting other ongoing projects, Dr. Jitendra Singh spoke about research integrating exosomal profiling and metabolomics to identify biomarkers for predicting Type 2 diabetes among women with a history of gestational diabetes; studies investigating the link between Type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), including the S100A6 pathway and development of a potential neutralising monoclonal antibody; and research on hyperinsulinemia, hepatic SIRT1 and systemic insulin resistance. He also referred to studies on ribosomal proteins and insulin signalling, and research exploring arachidonic acid for its potential to improve glucose regulation while protecting skeletal muscle against diabetes-associated atrophy.
The Minister cited emerging research on macrophage Gi signalling as a potential therapeutic target for obesity and Type 2 diabetes, including findings published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation in September 2026. He also referred to efforts towards developing temperature-resilient insulin to facilitate storage and transportation, as well as research by startups exploring oral insulin, underscoring the role of institutional support, technology development and risk-taking in advancing new healthcare solutions. India has also made progress in indigenous biosimilar development, including liraglutide and insulin Lispro, further strengthening the country's capabilities in affordable diabetes treatment.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India's population diversity, genomic research capabilities and expanding scientific infrastructure offer immense opportunities for high-impact medical research. Referring to the India Genome Study involving 10,000 individuals across 84 population groups, he said the country's genetic diversity can provide an important scientific resource for advancing precision medicine and contributing to healthcare research globally.
Calling for greater public awareness and responsible scientific communication, the Minister urged the medical and scientific fraternity to counter misinformation surrounding diabetes, obesity, nutrition and weight-loss treatments. He cautioned against misleading diet advice circulated by self-styled nutritionists, unscientific claims and the unprescribed use of drugs for obesity management, saying misinformation can cause greater harm than lack of information. He emphasised that credible scientific voices must actively engage with society to ensure that health decisions are guided by evidence and responsible medical advice.
With India aspiring towards Viksit Bharat by 2047 and nearly 70 per cent of its population below the age of 40, Dr. Jitendra Singh said protecting the health, energy and productive potential of the country's youth is a national priority. Preventing obesity and diabetes among young Indians, he said, must be viewed as a collective responsibility involving scientific institutions, medical professionals, policymakers and society at large, rather than being left to diabetologists or healthcare professionals alone.
The Minister encouraged RSSDI and the wider medical research community to deepen engagement with India's ongoing scientific initiatives, strengthen research partnerships and contribute to the development of preventive, affordable and next-generation healthcare solutions, saying that the country's scientific progress in diabetes and metabolic health can also contribute to the larger national mission of building a Viksit Bharat.

title: A new recipe to shape magnetisation that could open new doors to storing quantum information
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                20 NOV 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Scientists have cracked a way to tune an exotic form of quantum magnetism in a network by changing the connectivity of the network. This may have applications in quantum devices, for example, in storing quantum information.
Many systems are composed of interacting objects, and that can range from gas in the room to social networks. The hub-and-spoke diagrams showing flight routes in aeroplane magazines illustrate how connectivity allows people to move across cities. Another relatable example is that of superspreaders during COVID, who acted as hubs in spreading the disease.
These are familiar instances that show how different patterns of connections can determine collective behaviour. But these are all classical systems.
A team from the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an Autonomous Institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), explored what happens when many quantum objects interact with each other, what sets the collective ordering and how the quantum units organise themselves.
To understand the system,
Revathy B. S.
, the lead author of the
new study
and a postdoctoral fellow at RRI, and
Shovan Dutta
, co-author and assistant professor in the Theoretical Physics group at RRI, pictured a square lattice with one vacant site (hole) and all other sites occupied by one electron.
Fig 1:
The top row shows the possible magnetic ordering of a many-body quantum system within a single square lattice. The bottom shows that the introduction of a diagonal in the square lattice yield
The electrons have an intrinsic property called spin, which can point up or down. The hole can hop from one site to another, and this motion of the hole can influence how the electron spins arrange themselves, giving rise to what scientists’ call “kinetic magnetism”. Unlike conventional magnetism which arises from direct interactions between the spins, kinetic magnetism arises from the quantum motion (kinetic energy) of particles. Kinetic magnetism is a true quantum-mechanical effect with no classical counterpart.
If all the spins point along the same direction, it is called ferromagnetic order, and if adjacent spins have opposite directions, it is called antiferromagnetic ordering. For a square lattice with one hole, it has been shown before that the lowest-energy state is ferromagnetic.
Revathy and Dutta showed that the magnetic ordering can be varied by the connectivity of the network. For example, introducing a diagonal bond in the square lattice makes the spins of the two electrons involved antiparallel, creating a quantum-mechanically anti-aligned pair of spins, called a “singlet”. The remaining sites retain the ferromagnetic ordering, and the hole keeps hopping across the network.
“What’s amazing is that I can almost deterministically predict that wherever I [introduce a diagonal bond], I will get [singlets],” said Revathy. By introducing a diagonal bond and changing the connectivity locally, they could engineer the global magnetic order. These findings demonstrate that collective quantum order can be shaped by geometry alone.
Fig 2:
Global magnetic order can not only be determined in a quantum many-body system, but also engineered
“This is far from obvious, because if you had a classical system, similar changes in geometry do not really affect the magnetic order,” said Dutta.
The computational complexity involved prevented physicists from tackling the problem for decades. A lattice with 20 sites yields a mind-boggling two million configurations. Revathy and Dutta used a combination of advanced numerical and analytical approaches to uncover these microscopic patterns and their physical origin.
The research published in Physical Review B is also particularly timely because experimental advances are reaching a stage where researchers can possibly observe the complex theory in action.
Although this work is theoretical, it opens new avenues for shaping quantum states of interacting particles, which may have applications in quantum devices. Our familiar hard drives, for example, use magnetic patterns to store information, but only as classical bits. The singlets in these networks are entangled quantum states and may be used to store quantum information.

https://doi.org/10.1103/stj9-srp1
